lessons.title: Bridge: who am I? Personal details, family and 'I have'
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I introduce myself fully and accurately for a GCSE speaking or writing task?
objectives: To understand how to give developed personal details using عِنْدِي / لَدَيَّ, numbers and agreement
successCriteria: All: give name, age, home and family in full sentences
Most: use عِنْدِي and لَدَيَّ with correct number agreement
Some: develop each answer with a reason, opinion or second time frame
lessons.crossCurricular: English: developing spoken answers (point, detail, opinion)
lessons.smsc: Social: speaking about family with respect and privacy

hook.text: An examiner asks: حَدِّثْنِي عَنْ نَفْسِكَ (Tell me about yourself). What makes a Grade 4 answer different from a Grade 8 answer?
hook.a: Range (connectives, tenses, opinions) and accuracy, not just length.

islamicLink.text: Allah made us peoples and tribes so that we may know one another (al-Hujurat 49:13). Introducing ourselves well is the first step in that.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'I live in London': A) أَسْكُنُ فِي لَنْدَنَ B) أَنَا لَنْدَنُ

starter.a: For example: عُمْرِي خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً

teach.heading: Personal details

head: Question
Answer
rows: عُمْرِي أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ / خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً
أَسْكُنُ فِي ... فِي شَمَالِ / جَنُوبِ إِنْجِلْتِرَا

teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Teach in Arabic where possible (about 70% this year). Pupils may describe a real or made-up family.

teach.heading: Two ways to say 'I have'
teach.note: Both take the owned thing in the nominative. Negative: لَيْسَ عِنْدِي / لَيْسَ لَدَيَّ.

teach.heading: Numbers and family
bullets: 1, 2: noun alone or dual: أَخٌ، أَخَوَانِ
3 to 10: plural, number flips gender: ثَلَاثَةُ إِخْوَةٍ، ثَلَاثُ أَخَوَاتٍ
11+: singular accusative: أَحَدَ عَشَرَ ابْنَ عَمٍّ
teach.note: Group A: name the rule in Arabic: العَدَدُ يُخَالِفُ المَعْدُودَ (3 to 10 take the opposite gender).

teach.heading: Model: a developed answer

model.problem: حَدِّثْنِي عَنْ أُسْرَتِكَ.
steps: Point: فِي أُسْرَتِي خَمْسَةُ أَشْخَاصٍ.
Detail: لَدَيَّ أَخَوَانِ وَأُخْتٌ وَاحِدَةٌ.
Opinion and reason: أَنَا قَرِيبٌ مِنْ أَخِي الكَبِيرِ لِأَنَّهُ يُسَاعِدُنِي.
Second time frame: عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا، كُنَّا نَلْعَبُ مَعًا.
model.answer: Four linked sentences with range

teach.note: This is the shape for the 1AA0 conversation and for 4AA1 writing.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: أُخْت is feminine, so 3 takes the masculine form ثَلَاثُ, with a plural noun.

practice.q: Answer in two developed sentences: أَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟
practice.a: For example: أَسْكُنُ فِي مَدِينَةِ لِيسْتَر فِي وَسَطِ إِنْجِلْتِرَا. أُحِبُّ مَدِينَتِي لِأَنَّهَا هَادِئَةٌ وَفِيهَا مَسَاجِدُ كَثِيرَةٌ.
practice.model:
Point: أَسْكُنُ فِي ...
Detail: where it is (فِي وَسَطِ إِنْجِلْتِرَا).
Opinion + reason: أُحِبُّ مَدِينَتِي لِأَنَّهَا ...

practice.q: Translate: I have two brothers but I do not have a sister.
practice.a: لَدَيَّ أَخَوَانِ لٰكِنْ لَيْسَ لَدَيَّ أُخْتٌ.

practice.q: Say: there are four people in my family.

independent.q: Core: Write 80 words (portal response box) answering: حَدِّثْنِي عَنْ نَفْسِكَ وَعَنْ أُسْرَتِكَ. Use عِنْدِي or لَدَيَّ, a number 3 to 10, an opinion and a reason.
independent.a: Marked for: personal details; family with correct number agreement; opinion with لِأَنَّ; connectives; accuracy.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first three sentences live, saying why each number form is chosen.

independent.q: Extend (Group B, 1AA0 conversation): answer aloud for one minute in a breakout room; partner notes connectives used.
independent.a: One-minute developed answer with at least three connectives

independent.q: Stretch (Group A, 4AA1 grammar): give the i'rab of أَخَوَانِ in لَدَيَّ أَخَوَانِ.
independent.a: مُبْتَدَأٌ مُؤَخَّرٌ مَرْفُوعٌ وَعَلَامَةُ رَفْعِهِ الأَلِفُ لِأَنَّهُ مُثَنًّى (delayed subject, nominative, marked by alif because it is dual)

exit.q: 'I have' (formal) is: A) لَدَيَّ B) لِي C) أَنَا
Big question: what makes an introduction score highly?
exit.a: Developed answers with opinions, reasons, connectives, more than one time frame and accurate agreement.

lessons.homework: Learn your 80-word answer for the conversation (Group B) or redraft it to 120 words with one more time frame (Group A).
lessons.send: SEND: answer frame with sentence starters. EAL: key phrase card. Stretch: add the past habit كُنْتُ + present verb.

lessons.title: Bridge: describing people: agreement, the dual and qualifiers
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I make a description of a person precise and accurate?
objectives: To understand how adjectives agree in gender and number, including the dual, and how qualifiers make descriptions precise
successCriteria: All: describe appearance and character with agreeing adjectives
Most: use the dual correctly: لَهُ عَيْنَانِ بُنِّيَّتَانِ
Some: use qualifiers and a comparison in a paragraph
lessons.crossCurricular: English: precise vocabulary and modifiers (very, quite, rather)
lessons.smsc: Moral: good character (akhlaq) matters more than appearance

hook.text: Describe your best friend in three words. Did you choose looks or character? Which tells us more?
hook.a: Character tells us more about who someone is.

islamicLink.text: Allah praised the Prophet ﷺ: 'And indeed you are of a great moral character' (al-Qalam 68:4). In Islam, character is the best description of a person.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'I have two brothers': A) لَدَيَّ أَخَوَانِ B) لَدَيَّ اِثْنَانِ أَخٌ

teach.heading: Appearance and character
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Describe in words only; no pictures of people.

teach.heading: The dual
teach.note: Adjectives in the dual agree too: ـَانِ for both noun and adjective. Colours: خَضْرَاء → خَضْرَاوَانِ.

teach.heading: Qualifiers

head: Qualifier
Example
rows: هِيَ خَجُولَةٌ قَلِيلًا: a little shy
أَخِي طَوِيلٌ إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا: fairly tall

teach.note: Qualifiers come after the adjective.

teach.heading: Model: a paragraph

model.problem: صِفْ صَدِيقًا لَكَ (describe a friend).
steps: صَدِيقِي عُمَرُ طَوِيلٌ إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا وَلَهُ شَعْرٌ أَسْوَدُ قَصِيرٌ.
هُوَ مَرِحٌ جِدًّا وَكَرِيمٌ.
هُوَ أَطْوَلُ مِنِّي لٰكِنَّهُ أَصْغَرُ مِنِّي.
أُحِبُّهُ لِأَنَّهُ يُسَاعِدُ الآخَرِينَ دَائِمًا.
model.answer: Appearance, character, comparison, opinion

teach.note: Mark each feature: qualifier, comparison, reason.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: Dual noun, dual adjective: أُخْتَانِ لَطِيفَتَانِ.

practice.q: Describe a cheerful, fairly tall female cousin.
practice.a: بِنْتُ عَمِّي مَرِحَةٌ وَطَوِيلَةٌ إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا.
practice.model:
Noun: بِنْتُ عَمِّي (feminine).
Adjectives with ة: مَرِحَةٌ، طَوِيلَةٌ.
Qualifier after: إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا.

practice.q: Make dual: لَهُ عَيْنٌ زَرْقَاءُ.
What does خَجُول mean?

independent.q: Core: Write 70 to 90 words (portal response box): صِفْ شَخْصًا تُعْجَبُ بِهِ (describe someone you admire), with appearance, character, a qualifier, a comparison and a reason.
independent.a: Marked for agreement (gender, dual), qualifiers, comparison with أَفْعَل مِنْ, opinion with reason.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first two sentences about an imaginary teacher.

independent.q: Extend (Group B): prepare a 30-second spoken description for the picture-based task style: يَبْدُو ... (he seems ...).
independent.a: For example: يَبْدُو سَعِيدًا وَمَرِحًا.

independent.q: Stretch (Group A): give the i'rab of طَوِيلٌ in صَدِيقِي طَوِيلٌ.
independent.a: خَبَرٌ مَرْفُوعٌ وَعَلَامَةُ رَفْعِهِ الضَّمَّةُ (predicate, nominative, marked by dammah)

exit.q: What does إِلَى حَدٍّ مَا mean? A) fairly B) very C) never
Big question: what makes a description precise?
exit.a: Agreeing adjectives (including dual), qualifiers and comparisons.

lessons.homework: Write a description of two people (dual) you know, e.g. two cousins, with qualifiers.
lessons.send: SEND: adjective bank with m / f / dual forms. EAL: English beside each. Stretch: the plural of adjectives for people: طِوَالٌ، كِرَامٌ.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Identity and culture - Who am I?
lessons.title: Friends and relationships
objectives: Talk about friends and why they matter
Use verbs of relationships in the present tense
Give opinions with reasons about friendship
starter: Describe a person in two sentences.
Translate: 'My father is tall and kind'.
Say how many people are in your family.

teach.heading: My best friend
bullets: صَدِيقِي الْمُفَضَّلُ اسْمُهُ عُمَرُ - my favourite friend is called Umar
نَلْتَقِي كُلَّ يَوْمٍ - naltaqī kulla yawmin - we meet every day
أَقْضِي وَقْتًا مَعَهُ - I spend time with him
هُوَ مُخْلِصٌ وَصَادِقٌ - he is loyal and honest
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Introduce the word 'favourite' as الْمُفَضَّلُ. Pupils describe their best friend using vocabulary from Lesson 2. Online learning means friends may be in different places; invite pupils to describe friends in different cities. Respect privacy: no real names if they prefer.

teach.heading: What makes a good friend?
bullets: هُوَ يَسْمَعُنِي - he listens to me
لَا يَكْذِبُ - he does not lie
teach.note: Link to the Islamic ethic of brotherhood and sisterhood. Qur'an 49:10: the believers are but brothers, so make peace between them. Practise using the verbs in sentences. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said none of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Disagreements
bullets: ثُمَّ نَتَصَالَحُ - thumma natasālaḥu - then we make up
teach.note: Teach the vocabulary for conflict resolution and use it in sentences. Ask: why is forgiveness important? The Prophet (peace be upon him) said it is not lawful for a Muslim to avoid his brother for more than three nights, and the better of the two is the one who greets first (Bukhari and Muslim).

teach.heading: Giving opinions on friendship
bullets: فِي رَأْيِي الصَّدَاقَةُ مُهِمَّةٌ - fī ra'yī aṣ-ṣadāqatu muhimma
لِأَنَّ الصَّدِيقَ يُسَاعِدُنِي - because a friend helps me
الْأَصْدِقَاءُ الصَّالِحُونَ مُهِمُّونَ - good friends are important
teach.note: Combine opinion + reason. Use plural agreement: الْأَصْدِقَاءُ الصَّالِحُونَ (sound masculine plural adjective). Model extended answers. Pupils practise a mini-conversation about friendship.

teach.heading: Speaking practice
bullets: هَلْ لَدَيْكَ أَصْدِقَاءُ كَثِيرُونَ؟ - do you have many friends?
مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِكَ؟ - what do you do with your friends?
كَيْفَ هُوَ الصَّدِيقُ الْجَيِّدُ؟ - what is a good friend like?
teach.note: Pupils practise a three-question conversation in pairs. Remind them to give full answers and add detail. Collect examples of good answers. Assess pronunciation and fluency informally.

practice: Say two qualities of a good friend.
Translate: 'We help each other and we trust each other'.
Say: 'Sometimes we argue but then we make up'.
Ask a partner: 'What do you do with your friends?'
independent: Write a 70-word text about your best friend and why you like them.
Role-play a conversation about friendship with a partner.
Record a one-minute speaking answer on 'A good friend'.
exit: Write one sentence about a good friend with a reason.
Say 'I apologise' and 'I forgive him' in Arabic.
lessons.homework: Write a 90-word paragraph on 'Friendship is important', with two reasons and one example.
lessons.send: SEND: sentence builders on friendship. EAL: bilingual relationship vocabulary. Stretch: give a short opinion on online friendships using عَبْرَ الْإِنْتَرْنِتِ.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Identity and culture - Who am I?
lessons.title: Writing about myself, my family and friends
objectives: Plan and write a structured paragraph
Use a range of structures and linking words
Edit your own work for accuracy
starter: Say one sentence about a friend with a reason.
Describe your sister's appearance in Arabic.
Say 'I trust him' and 'we help each other' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Plan the paragraph
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Explain that a strong piece of writing in the exam is organised. Use a planning grid: who, what, why. Pupils plan on a mini-whiteboard. Show how to use ideas from Lessons 1–3.

teach.heading: Model paragraph
bullets: اسْمِي عَائِشَةُ وَعُمْرِي أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً - I am 14
لِي أَخَوَانِ وَأُخْتٌ وَاحِدَةٌ - I have two brothers and one sister
teach.note: Read aloud and gloss. Identify the structures: age, home, family, reason. Ask: what would improve the paragraph? Possible answers: more detail, opinion, connectives. Note: ʿumrī ... sanatan with 14 in the feminine form (أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ).

teach.heading: Linking words
teach.note: Teach connectives that give the writing a formal tone. Pupils replace وَ with a better connective in the model. Encourage variety. Avoid overuse of one structure. Link to ihsan: strive for excellence.

teach.heading: Editing checklist
teach.note: Teach a four-step checklist. Pupils correct a flawed paragraph containing five errors: غُرْفَةٌ كَبِيرٌ, عُمْرِي خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً, هِيَ يَذْهَبُ, الصَّدِيقَةُ مُخْلِصٌ, أَسْكُنُ فِي لَنْدَنٍ. Ask which errors are the most serious.

teach.heading: Exam writing tips
teach.note: Practise a writing question: 'Describe yourself, your family and your friends.' Plan in four bullets and write 90 words. Remind about timing: 5 minutes planning, 20 minutes writing, 5 minutes checking.

practice: Correct: عُمْرِي خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً.
Join the sentences with لِأَنَّ: أُحِبُّ أُخْتِي / هِيَ لَطِيفَةٌ.
Add a connective: أَسْكُنُ فِي لَنْدَنَ ___ أُحِبُّ الْمَدِينَةَ.
Translate: 'In addition, my friend is loyal'.
independent: Write a 90-word paragraph on 'Myself, my family and my friends'.
Swap with a partner and use the checklist.
Rewrite your paragraph with corrections.
exit: Write one sentence with 'therefore'.
List two items from the editing checklist.
lessons.homework: Redraft your paragraph and prepare to speak it aloud without notes.
lessons.send: SEND: paragraph skeleton and word bank. EAL: bilingual connective list. Stretch: add a comparison between two family members.

lessons.bigQuestion: How do I describe daily life for me and for others in the present tense?
objectives: To understand how the present tense changes for each person and how to describe routines with frequency words
successCriteria: All: describe my routine with five present-tense verbs
Most: conjugate a verb for I, you, he, she, we and they
Some: compare my routine with someone else's using frequency words
lessons.crossCurricular: PSHE: healthy routines, sleep and screen time
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: a Muslim day organised around the five prayers

hook.text: How is a Muslim teenager's day shaped differently from that of someone who does not pray? Think of the times.
hook.a: Fajr before school, Dhuhr and Asr in the day, Maghrib and Isha in the evening shape the routine.

islamicLink.text: Allah says prayer is prescribed at fixed times (an-Nisa' 4:103). The five prayers give a Muslim's day its shape.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'Very' is: A) جِدًّا B) قَلِيلًا

teach.heading: One verb, all persons
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Prefixes أَ، تَ، يَ، نَ; suffixes ـِينَ and ـُونَ. Group A: the term حُرُوفُ المُضَارَعَةِ (أَنَيْتُ).

teach.heading: My routine
bullets: أَتَنَاوَلُ الفَطُورَ ثُمَّ أَبْدَأُ دُرُوسِي عَبْرَ الإِنْتَرْنِتِ
فِي المَسَاءِ أُرَاجِعُ القُرْآنَ وَأَنَامُ مُبَكِّرًا
teach.note: Add time phrases: فِي الصَّبَاحِ، بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ، فِي المَسَاءِ.

teach.heading: How often?
teach.note: أَبَدًا needs a negative before the verb.

teach.heading: Model: comparing routines

model.problem: Compare my routine and my brother's.
steps: أَنَا أَسْتَيْقِظُ مُبَكِّرًا عَادَةً،
لٰكِنَّ أَخِي يَسْتَيْقِظُ مُتَأَخِّرًا أَحْيَانًا.
نَحْنُ نُصَلِّي الفَجْرَ مَعًا دَائِمًا.
هُمْ (my cousins) يَدْرُسُونَ فِي مَدْرَسَةٍ قَرِيبَةٍ.
model.answer: Four persons, three frequency words

teach.note: Range of persons = higher marks.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: أَنْتِ takes تَـ ... ـِينَ: تَدْرُسِينَ.

practice.q: Conjugate يَكْتُبُ for نَحْنُ and هُمْ.
practice.model:
نَحْنُ takes نَـ: نَكْتُبُ.
هُمْ takes يَـ ... ـُونَ: يَكْتُبُونَ.

practice.q: Translate: I usually go to bed at ten.
Say 'I never arrive late'.

independent.q: Core: Write 80 words on a typical weekday (portal response box), with five verbs, three frequency words and the prayers.
independent.a: Marked for range of verbs, frequency words, time phrases and accuracy.
independent.model: Teacher writes the morning part live: أَسْتَيْقِظُ قَبْلَ الفَجْرِ ...

independent.q: Extend: Add three sentences about another person (أَخِي، أُمِّي، أَصْدِقَائِي) with the right verb forms.
independent.a: For example: أُمِّي تَطْبُخُ الغَدَاءَ. أَصْدِقَائِي يَلْعَبُونَ بَعْدَ المَدْرَسَةِ.

independent.q: Stretch (Group A): identify the حَرْفُ المُضَارَعَةِ in four verbs from your answer and name the person each shows.
independent.a: For example: نَـ in نُصَلِّي (we); يَـ in يَلْعَبُونَ (they)

exit.q: 'They study': A) يَدْرُسُونَ B) نَدْرُسُ C) تَدْرُسُ
Big question: how does the present tense change for different people?
exit.a: Prefixes (أَ، تَ، يَ، نَ) and suffixes (ـِينَ، ـُونَ) show who does the action.

lessons.homework: Conjugate يَشْرَبُ and يَلْعَبُ for all eight persons; write five sentences about your family's routine.
lessons.send: SEND: conjugation grid with prefixes highlighted. EAL: routine pictures (objects and clocks). Stretch: verbs with weak letters: يَنَامُ، يَمْشِي.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Identity and culture - Daily life
lessons.title: Food, mealtimes and healthy eating
objectives: Talk about meals and eating habits
Give opinions about healthy and unhealthy food
Use comparisons and reasons in Arabic
starter: Say what you do in the morning and evening.
Say a sentence with 'sometimes' and a verb.
Name three foods in Arabic.

teach.heading: Meals
bullets: أَتَنَاوَلُ الْفُطُورَ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ - I eat breakfast at seven
نَتَنَاوَلُ الْغَدَاءَ مَعًا - we have lunch together
الْعَشَاءُ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ مَسَاءً - dinner at 7pm
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Revise food vocabulary from Year 9. Ask pupils what they eat for each meal. The Prophet (peace be upon him) advised his companions to gather over their food and mention Allah's name so that there is blessing in it (Abu Dawud). The basic point is that eating together builds family bonds.

teach.heading: Healthy and unhealthy
bullets: الْخُضَارُ وَالْفَاكِهَةُ مُفِيدَةٌ لِلصِّحَّةِ - vegetables and fruit are good
الْوَجَبَاتُ السَّرِيعَةُ ضَارَّةٌ بِالصِّحَّةِ - fast food is bad
teach.note: Plural things take a feminine singular adjective: الْوَجَبَاتُ السَّرِيعَةُ ضَارَّةٌ. Note ضَارٌّ with shadda. Ask pupils to classify foods into healthy and unhealthy. Include halal and tayyib: Qur'an 2:168 'eat of what is lawful and good'.

teach.heading: Moderation
bullets: كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا - eat and drink and do not waste
أُحَاوِلُ أَنْ آكُلَ طَعَامًا صِحِّيًّا - I try to eat healthy food
teach.note: Qur'an 7:31: eat and drink but do not be extravagant. Link to health and not wasting food. Teach أُحَاوِلُ أَنْ + subjunctive. Pupils say one change they could make to be healthier.

teach.heading: Giving advice
bullets: يَجِبُ أَنْ نَشْرَبَ الْمَاءَ - we must drink water
يَجِبُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ الْخُضَارَ - we must eat vegetables
لَا يَجِبُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْوَجَبَاتِ السَّرِيعَةِ
teach.note: Teach يَجِبُ أَنْ (it is necessary to) + verb with fatḥa. Practise giving advice to a friend. Also teach يُفَضَّلُ أَنْ (it is preferable to). Ask pupils to write three pieces of advice.

teach.heading: Speaking and writing
bullets: مَاذَا تَأْكُلُ عَادَةً؟ - what do you usually eat?
هَلْ تَأْكُلُ طَعَامًا صِحِّيًّا؟ - do you eat healthy food?
teach.note: Practise three-question conversation. Model a full answer: 'I usually eat rice and chicken. I try to eat vegetables because they are good for health.' Pupils practise with a partner and swap.

practice: Say what you eat for breakfast and why.
Translate: 'Fast food is bad for health'.
Give advice using يَجِبُ أَنْ.
Say the Arabic for 'I try to eat healthy food'.
independent: Write a 80-word text on healthy eating with advice and reasons.
Make a survey of three people's food habits and report in Arabic.
Prepare a 1-minute talk 'Food in my life'.
exit: Write one sentence with يَجِبُ أَنْ.
Write one unhealthy food and one healthy food.
lessons.homework: Write a leaflet in Arabic (90 words) giving advice for a healthy diet, with at least four pieces of advice.
lessons.send: SEND: food cards with healthy/unhealthy labels. EAL: bilingual vocabulary with audio. Stretch: add comparisons, for example الْمَاءُ أَفْضَلُ مِنَ الْعَصِيرِ (water is better than juice).

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Identity and culture - Daily life
lessons.title: Technology and social media
objectives: Talk about technology and how we use it
Give advantages and disadvantages
Express and justify opinions about social media
starter: Give advice about healthy food using يَجِبُ أَنْ.
Say what you usually eat for lunch.
Translate: 'Water is important'.

teach.heading: What I use
bullets: أَسْتَعْمِلُ الْهَاتِفَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ - I use my phone every day
أَسْتَعْمِلُ الْحَاسُوبَ لِلدِّرَاسَةِ - I use the computer for study
أَلْعَبُ الْأَلْعَابَ الْإِلِكْتْرُونِيَّةَ - I play video games
أَتَوَاصَلُ مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِي - I communicate with friends
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Introduce vocabulary and ask how pupils use technology. Remind them that use of phones for learning is a good use. Note the verb أَسْتَعْمِلُ (form X). The ل in لِلدِّرَاسَةِ means 'for'. Pupils give three uses.

teach.heading: Advantages
bullets: التِّكْنُولُوجْيَا تُسَهِّلُ الْحَيَاةَ - technology makes life easier
نَتَعَلَّمُ عَبْرَ الْإِنْتَرْنِتِ - we learn online
نَتَوَاصَلُ مَعَ الْعَائِلَةِ فِي الْخَارِجِ - with family abroad
teach.note: Elicit positive uses: learning, communication, saving time. Online school is itself an example. Use the connectors أَوَّلًا and ثَانِيًا (secondly). Pupils write three advantages.

teach.heading: Disadvantages
bullets: الْإِدْمَانُ عَلَى الْهَاتِفِ - addiction to the phone
قَدْ يَكُونُ خَطِيرًا - it may be dangerous
teach.note: Discuss risks: wasting time, addiction, bullying, strangers and privacy. Connect to online safety taught in PSHE. Use the word قَدْ + present (may). Remind pupils of the hadith about two blessings many people lose: health and free time (Sahih al-Bukhari).

teach.heading: Giving a balanced opinion
bullets: مِنْ جِهَةٍ هُوَ مُفِيدٌ - on the one hand it is useful
وَمِنْ جِهَةٍ أُخْرَى هُوَ خَطِيرٌ - on the other hand it is dangerous
فِي رَأْيِي يَجِبُ أَنْ نَسْتَعْمِلَهُ بِحِكْمَةٍ - wisely
teach.note: Teach the pair مِنْ جِهَةٍ ... وَمِنْ جِهَةٍ أُخْرَى. Practise balanced answers. Pupils say 'in my opinion we must use it wisely'. Highlight بِحِكْمَةٍ (with wisdom).

teach.heading: Mini debate
bullets: كَمْ سَاعَةً تَسْتَعْمِلُ الْهَاتِفَ؟ - how many hours?
هَلْ هُوَ مُفِيدٌ أَمْ ضَارٌّ؟ - useful or harmful?
teach.note: Pupils debate in pairs: one argues for, one against. Use opinion phrases. Collect points and write them on the board. Encourage respectful disagreement.

practice: Name three uses of a phone.
Give one advantage and one disadvantage of social media.
Translate: 'In my opinion we must use it wisely'.
Say how many hours you use your phone.
independent: Write a balanced paragraph of 90 words on social media.
Prepare a debate: 'Technology makes our life better'.
Record a 1-minute speaking answer.
exit: Write one advantage of technology.
Write one disadvantage and a piece of advice.
lessons.homework: Write a 100-word opinion article in Arabic: 'Technology and young people'.
lessons.send: SEND: advantages and disadvantages matching cards. EAL: bilingual vocabulary list. Stretch: add a conditional sentence with إِذَا.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Identity and culture - Daily life
lessons.title: Free time, sport and hobbies
objectives: Describe free-time activities and sport
Use the present, past and future tenses together
Explain why activities are important for health
starter: Give one advantage of technology in Arabic.
Say how often you use your phone.
Translate: 'My hobby is reading'.

teach.heading: Hobbies
bullets: هِوَايَتِي الْقِرَاءَةُ - hiwāyatī al-qirā'a - my hobby is reading
أُحِبُّ الرَّسْمَ - uḥibbu r-rasm - I like drawing
أَقْضِي وَقْتَ فَرَاغِي فِي الْقِرَاءَةِ - I spend my free time reading
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Build on Y7 hobbies. Introduce the verbal noun (masdar): الْقِرَاءَةُ, الرَّسْمُ, الطَّبْخُ. Use أَقْضِي وَقْتَ فَرَاغِي فِي + masdar as a chunk. Note the genitive after فِي. Pupils write their own hobby sentence.

teach.heading: Sport
bullets: أَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ - I play football
أَسْبَحُ فِي الْمَسْبَحِ - I swim in the pool
أُمَارِسُ الرِّيَاضَةَ ثَلَاثَ مَرَّاتٍ فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ - three times a week
teach.note: Teach sports: كُرَةُ الْقَدَمِ, كُرَةُ السَّلَّةِ, السِّبَاحَةُ, الْجَرْيُ (running). The hadith: the strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, while there is good in both (Sahih Muslim). Link to taking care of the body.

teach.heading: Past and future
bullets: أَمْسِ لَعِبْتُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ - yesterday I played football
غَدًا سَأَسْبَحُ - tomorrow I will swim
فِي الْعُطْلَةِ سَنَلْعَبُ فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ - in the holiday we will play
teach.note: Combine tenses: present for habits, past for yesterday, future for plans. Pupils produce one sentence in each tense. Use a three-column table. Revise the past tense endings from Y8 and the future from Y9.

teach.heading: Why it matters
bullets: الرِّيَاضَةُ مُفِيدَةٌ لِلصِّحَّةِ - sport is good for health
تُقَوِّي الْجِسْمَ - it strengthens the body
teach.note: Teach the benefits. Note that الرِّيَاضَةُ is feminine and so the adjective is feminine. Connect to mental health: PSHE topic. Pupils choose one benefit and explain it in a sentence.

teach.heading: Speaking task
bullets: مَاذَا فَعَلْتَ فِي نِهَايَةِ الْأُسْبُوعِ الْمَاضِي؟
teach.note: Role-play with three tenses in questions. Pupils answer using the same tense as the question. Highlight how the question tells you which tense to use. Give feedback on accuracy.

practice: Say your hobby in Arabic.
Translate: 'I play football three times a week'.
Say what you did yesterday and what you will do tomorrow.
Give one benefit of sport.
independent: Write a 90-word text about your free time using all three tenses.
Interview a partner about their hobbies and write 5 sentences.
Prepare a 1-minute presentation.
exit: Write a sentence with أُمَارِسُ الرِّيَاضَةَ.
Write a sentence in the future about sport.
lessons.homework: Write a short article for a school magazine (100 words) on 'Free time and health'.
lessons.send: SEND: hobby pictures with verbs. EAL: bilingual hobby list. Stretch: add a comparison between two sports.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Local area, holiday and travel: town, region and country; holidays (2.3, 2.1)
lessons.title: Bridge: cultural life: Ramadan and Eid in three time frames
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I describe Ramadan and Eid using past, present and future?
objectives: To understand how to describe Ramadan and Eid using past, present and future verbs accurately
successCriteria: All: describe Ramadan in the present: نَصُومُ مِنَ الفَجْرِ إِلَى المَغْرِبِ
Most: say what I did last Eid and will do this Ramadan
Some: use three time frames and an opinion in one paragraph
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: the lunar calendar and moon sighting
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: the purpose of fasting is taqwa

hook.text: Ramadan starts in about three weeks. What will be the same as last year, and what do you want to do differently?
hook.a: Pupils' own; the goal of fasting is taqwa (al-Baqarah 2:183).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'O you who believe, fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, so that you may attain taqwa' (al-Baqarah 2:183). Ramadan is the month in which the Qur'an was sent down (al-Baqarah 2:185).

starter.q: Bismillah. 'We study': A) نَدْرُسُ B) يَدْرُسُونَ
Name the two Eids in Arabic.

teach.heading: Ramadan now (present)
bullets: نَتَسَحَّرُ قَبْلَ الفَجْرِ وَنُفْطِرُ عَلَى التَّمْرِ
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Hollow verb صَامَ / يَصُومُ: watch the long vowel.

teach.heading: Three time frames
teach.note: Hollow verbs shorten the long vowel in the past with ـتُ: صَامَ → صُمْتُ, زَارَ → زُرْتُ.

teach.heading: Eid
bullets: فِي العِيدِ نُصَلِّي صَلَاةَ العِيدِ وَنَلْبَسُ مَلَابِسَ جَدِيدَةً
teach.note: Spec 1.3 festivals are taught through Ramadan and the two Eids.

teach.heading: Model: a three-tense paragraph

model.problem: صِفْ رَمَضَانَ وَالعِيدَ فِي أُسْرَتِكَ.
steps: Present: فِي رَمَضَانَ نَصُومُ وَنُفْطِرُ مَعًا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
Past: فِي العِيدِ المَاضِي زُرْنَا جَدَّتِي وَكَانَ يَوْمًا رَائِعًا.
Future: هٰذِهِ السَّنَةَ سَأَقْرَأُ القُرْآنَ كُلَّهُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ.
Opinion: أُحِبُّ رَمَضَانَ لِأَنَّهُ شَهْرُ القُرْآنِ.
model.answer: Three time frames plus opinion

teach.note: This is a typical 1AA0 Paper 4 and 4AA1 Paper 2 topic.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: Hollow verb: the long ا drops and the first vowel becomes u: صُمْتُ.

practice.q: Translate: Last Eid we visited my grandparents.
practice.a: فِي العِيدِ المَاضِي زُرْنَا جَدِّي وَجَدَّتِي.
practice.model:
Time phrase: فِي العِيدِ المَاضِي.
Past 'we' of زَارَ: زُرْنَا.
Object: جَدِّي وَجَدَّتِي.

practice.q: Make future: نُصَلِّي التَّرَاوِيحَ.
What is سُحُور?

independent.q: Core: Write 90 words (portal response box): كَيْفَ تَقْضِي رَمَضَانَ وَالعِيدَ؟ Use three time frames and two opinions.
independent.a: Marked for three time frames (including hollow verbs), festival vocabulary, opinions with reasons and accuracy.
independent.model: Teacher writes the present-tense opening, then the past sentence.

independent.q: Extend (Group B): answer aloud: مَاذَا فَعَلْتَ فِي العِيدِ المَاضِي؟ (unexpected question practice).
independent.a: Developed past-tense answer

independent.q: Stretch (Group A): give the i'rab of رَائِعًا in كَانَ العِيدُ رَائِعًا.
independent.a: خَبَرُ كَانَ مَنْصُوبٌ وَعَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ الفَتْحَةُ (predicate of kana, accusative, marked by fathah)

exit.q: What is إِفْطَار? A) breaking the fast B) the night prayer C) charity
Big question: write one sentence about Ramadan in each time frame.

lessons.homework: Write a Ramadan goals list in Arabic in the future tense (five goals with إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ).
lessons.send: SEND: three-column verb card. EAL: festival word mat. Stretch: use كُنَّا + present for past habits: كُنَّا نُفْطِرُ مَعًا.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Identity and culture - Cultural life and exam skills
lessons.title: Customs, traditions and reading skills
objectives: Read a short text about family traditions
Use reading strategies to answer questions
Write a response about your own traditions
starter: Say a sentence about Eid in the past tense.
Greet someone on Eid in Arabic.
What do we call the meal before dawn?

teach.heading: Reading text
bullets: فِي بَيْتِنَا نَجْتَمِعُ كُلَّ يَوْمِ جُمُعَةٍ - we gather every Friday
تَطْبُخُ جَدَّتِي الْكُسْكُسِيَّ - my grandmother cooks couscous
يَلْعَبُ الْأَوْلَادُ وَيَشْرَبُ الْكِبَارُ الشَّايَ - children play, adults drink tea
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Read the text aloud, then ask for the gist. Pupils highlight verbs and identify the subjects. The text is in the present tense and describes habits. Introduce the vocabulary: نَجْتَمِعُ (we gather), الْكِبَارُ (adults).

teach.heading: Skimming and scanning
bullets: Skim: what is the text about?
Scan: find the detail you need
teach.note: Show the questions: مَتَى؟ (when?), مَنْ؟ (who?), مَاذَا؟ (what?), أَيْنَ؟ (where?). Model finding the answer to 'What does grandmother cook?' Teach pupils to underline the sentence with the answer. Explain how to avoid distractors.

teach.heading: Using context
teach.note: If pupils see an unknown word, they should use the root and context. For example, نَجْتَمِعُ comes from the root ج م ع, as in جَمِيعًا and جُمُعَة (gathering). The Friday gathering is a link to the Jumuʿa. Pupils guess one new word from context in a second text.

teach.heading: Customs and respect
bullets: نُسَاعِدُ الْكِبَارَ - nusāʿidu l-kibār - we help the elders
نُسَلِّمُ عَلَى الْجَمِيعِ - we greet everyone
teach.note: Link to the Islamic emphasis on kinship ties (silat al-rahim) and respect for elders. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that he is not one of us who does not show mercy to our young and respect our elders (Tirmidhi). Pupils describe a custom in their family.

teach.heading: My family traditions
bullets: فِي عَائِلَتِي عَادَةٌ - in my family there is a custom
نَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ كُلَّ ... - we do that every ...
teach.note: Give a frame to write about a tradition. Pupils write 3–4 sentences. They may choose any family or community custom, for example weekly gatherings, Eid breakfast or Qur'an on Friday.

practice: Answer in English: When does the family gather?
Find a verb in the text and say who it refers to.
What does 'الْكِبَارُ' mean?
Translate: 'My grandmother cooks and we eat together'.
independent: Read: فِي حَفْلَةِ الزَّوَاجِ تَجْتَمِعُ الْعَائِلَتَانِ فِي قَاعَةٍ كَبِيرَةٍ. يَلْبَسُ الْعَرِيسُ ثَوْبًا أَبْيَضَ وَتَلْبَسُ الْعَرُوسُ فُسْتَانًا جَمِيلًا. بَعْدَ الْعَشَاءِ يَدْعُو الضُّيُوفُ لَهُمَا بِالْبَرَكَةِ. Answer in English: where do the families meet, what does the groom wear, and what happens after dinner?
Write a 70-word text about a custom in your family.
Create three comprehension questions for a partner.
exit: Name the question word for 'when'.
Write a sentence about a family tradition.
lessons.homework: Write an 80-word text about a tradition in your family and learn eight new words.
lessons.send: SEND: text with glossary and picture support. EAL: bilingual glossary. Stretch: translate the text into English in full sentences.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Identity and culture - Cultural life and exam skills
lessons.title: Listening skills and exam practice
objectives: Use strategies to answer listening questions
Recognise numbers, times and dates
Answer in the correct form
starter: Name the question words for 'when' and 'where'.
Say 'we gather every Friday'.
Say the time 8:45 in Arabic.

teach.heading: Before listening
bullets: اقْرَأِ الْأَسْئِلَةَ أَوَّلًا - read the questions first
اِنْتَبِهْ إِلَى الْأَرْقَامِ - note the numbers
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. In the Listening paper recordings are normally played more than once (check the current specification). Use the first listening for the gist and the next to check the details. Predict vocabulary based on the question. Remind pupils that Arabic recordings may use different accents.

teach.heading: Numbers and times
bullets: فِي الْخَامِسِ مِنْ نُوفَمْبَرَ - on 5 November
teach.note: Practise recognising numbers. Dictate numbers and times for pupils to write in digits. Cover dates: الْيَوْمُ + ordinal number + مِنْ + month. Note months: يَنَايِرُ, فِبْرَايِرُ, مَارِسُ, أَبْرِيلُ, مَايُو, يُونْيُو, يُولْيُو, أُغُسْطُسُ, سِبْتَمْبَرُ, أُكْتُوبَرُ, نُوفَمْبَرُ, دِيسَمْبَرُ (Levantine/Western names). Use the Gregorian months and the Islamic months as a comparison.

teach.heading: Distractors
bullets: لَيْسَ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ بَلْ يَوْمَ الثُّلَاثَاءِ - not Monday but Tuesday
عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ - ʿalā kulli ḥālin - anyway
فِي الْبِدَايَةِ ... لَكِنْ ... - at first ... but ...
teach.note: Explain that recordings often include a change of mind: 'not on Monday but on Tuesday'. Listen for لَيْسَ ... بَلْ ..., لَكِنْ, وَلَكِنْ and عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ. Teach that the answer is often after the contrast word. Practise with a short dictation.

teach.heading: Practice
bullets: The teacher reads a short recording twice
teach.note: Read a short script aloud twice at normal speed. Sample: 'مَرْحَبًا، اسْمِي سَلْمَى. عُمْرِي أَرْبَعَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً. أَسْكُنُ فِي مَانْشِسْتَر مَعَ أَبِي وَأُمِّي وَأَخِي. هِوَايَتِي السِّبَاحَةُ، أَسْبَحُ كُلَّ يَوْمِ سَبْتٍ فِي السَّاعَةِ الْعَاشِرَةِ.' Ask: age, city, hobby, day and time.

teach.heading: Reviewing mistakes
teach.note: Review exam technique: a listening answer must be specific and relevant. Show how an answer like 'swimming on Saturday at ten' is complete. Pupils reflect on the answer they gave and why they lost marks. Make a class list of tips.

practice: Listen to the numbers I read and write them as digits.
Listen to two times and write them.
What does 'لَيْسَ ... بَلْ' signal?
Translate: 'on 5 November'.
independent: Listen to the recording read by the teacher and answer five questions.
Make your own short script of 40 words and test a partner.
Write a list of five tips for the Listening paper.
exit: Give two tips for the listening exam.
Write the time 4:30 in Arabic.
lessons.homework: Listen to an Arabic news bulletin or short video (5 minutes) and write the topic and three details in English.
lessons.send: SEND: transcripts with gap-fills. EAL: bilingual tips. Stretch: write a recording script with a distractor and swap with a partner.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Identity and culture - Cultural life and exam skills
lessons.title: Assessment: speaking and writing
objectives: Complete a role play and a conversation on Identity and culture
Write a 120-word text using a range of structures
Evaluate your work against the mark scheme
starter: Say your name, age and family.
Give an opinion about technology.
Describe your daily routine in two sentences.

teach.heading: Assessment format
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Explain the three tasks. The role play is a simple scenario where pupils ask and answer questions. The conversation covers the themes studied: who am I, daily life, cultural life. The writing is a structured text. Show pupils the marking criteria in simple language.

teach.heading: Role-play model
bullets: أَنْتَ فِي مَطْعَمٍ - you are in a restaurant
اسْأَلْ عَنِ السِّعْرِ - ask the price
teach.note: Model the role-play in Arabic: customer and waiter. Highlight that pupils must respond to all points. Take care that your voice is clear. Practise a few question starters: كَمْ؟, مَاذَا؟, هَلْ؟.

teach.heading: Conversation tips
teach.note: Model a strong answer to 'Tell me about your family' and a weak one 'I have a brother'. Pupils extend weak answers. Use connectives and time expressions. Remind pupils to stay calm and to ask for repetition: أَعِدْ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.

teach.heading: Writing tips
teach.note: Show a model 120-word text on 'My life' with opinion, past and future. Pupils identify the features. Recall common errors from this phase: number agreement, adjective agreement, ة/ت. Give 5 minutes to plan.

teach.heading: Reflection
teach.note: Pupils reflect and write targets, for example 'use more complex structures', 'avoid repetition', 'check number agreement'. Praise effort. Close with الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ.

practice: Prepare answers: 'Tell me about your family'.
Prepare answers: 'What do you do in your free time?'
Prepare a role-play question: ask the price of an item.
independent: Complete the role play with a partner (2 minutes) and the conversation (3 minutes).
Write 120 words on 'My life and culture'.
Self-assess against the success criteria and set one target.
exit: Name one strength and one weakness in your Arabic.
Set a target for the next unit.
lessons.homework: Review and correct your writing, then learn ten words you misspelt or forgot.
lessons.send: SEND: sentence starters and a vocabulary mat. EAL: bilingual mark scheme. Stretch: extend the conversation with a conditional sentence using إِذَا.

lessons.unit: Unit 1.1: Who am I?
lessons.title: When I was younger: kāna and the past tense
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I talk about who I was as a child and how I have changed?
objectives: Conjugate كَانَ and a regular past-tense verb for all persons
Contrast a single past event with a past habit (used to)
Write 5 or more accurate sentences about childhood
successCriteria: All: use كُنْتُ / كَانَ / كَانَتْ with an adjective to describe a person in the past
Most: use كُنْتُ + present verb for 'used to' and conjugate دَرَسَ
Some: use the negative لَمْ أَكُنْ and link ideas with لِأَنَّ and لَكِنْ
lessons.crossCurricular: English: past tenses and 'used to'; Art: a still life of a childhood object
lessons.smsc: Moral: gratitude (shukr) for the people who raised us; Social: growing and changing

keywords.def: I was not / I did not use to (lam akun)

starter: Bismillah. Say in Arabic: my name, my age, where I live.
Write the Arabic for 'my father', 'my mother' and 'my sister' (with the 'my' ending).
Give three Arabic adjectives that describe a person.

teach.heading: كَانَ: was / were
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. This is the first lesson on 'what I was like when I was younger' (spec unit 1.1). Read the table aloud with pupils echoing. Point out that كَانَ is a verb, so what follows it (the adjective) is in the accusative with tanween: كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا. Ask: which forms end in a long ū with a silent alif? (هُمْ كَانُوا). Girls say كُنْتُ صَغِيرَةً. Note that the written exam does not require vowels, but pupils must hear and say the endings.

teach.heading: A regular past-tense verb
teach.note: Model with دَرَسَ (to study). The past tense is built from a stem plus endings, so once pupils know the endings they can conjugate any regular verb: كَتَبَ, لَعِبَ, سَكَنَ. Drill: teacher says a pronoun, pupils say the form. Common error: confusing -tu (I) with -ta (you m) and -ti (you f). Choral practice, then pair practice with mini-whiteboards.

teach.heading: One event or a habit?

left.title: Single past event
points: Yesterday I went to the market

right.title: Past habit: used to
points: I used to walk to school

teach.note: Contrast: past verb = something that happened (once or finished); كَانَ + present verb = a habit in the past (used to). This is a Higher-level feature and lifts speaking and writing. Ask pupils to find the verb pair in each sentence. Remind them that the verb after كَانَ is in the ordinary present tense (أَذْهَبُ), and that it agrees in person with كَانَ.

teach.heading: Model: describing my childhood

model.problem: Translate: 'When I was young, I lived in London and I used to walk to school.'
steps: 'When I was young' = عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا
'I lived' as a habit = كُنْتُ أَسْكُنُ + 'in London' = فِي لَنْدَنَ
'I used to walk' = وَكُنْتُ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ مَشْيًا
Join with a comma and wa- (and)
model.answer: عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا، كُنْتُ أَسْكُنُ فِي لَنْدَنَ وَكُنْتُ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ مَشْيًا

teach.note: Think aloud while building the sentence in three parts: (1) عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا = 'when I was young' (2) كُنْتُ أَسْكُنُ = 'I used to live' (3) the extra detail. Show how a time phrase plus a habit plus a reason makes a developed answer. Pupils copy the structure, then change the details.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which sentence means 'My brother was funny'?
check.why: كَانَ is masculine for a male subject and the adjective after it takes tanween fatha (مُضْحِكًا). A has no past verb; C has the feminine verb; D is first person.

teach.note: Show on mini-whiteboards, A to D. The trap options show the three commonest errors: present tense, the wrong gender of كَانَ, and the first person for a third-person subject. If many choose C, redo the verb-first agreement rule: with the verb before the subject, كَانَ agrees in gender only, and أَخِي is masculine.

practice: Fill the gap with the correct form of كَانَ: (a) ___ أَخِي صَغِيرًا (b) ___ أُمِّي مُعَلِّمَةً (c) نَحْنُ ___ أَصْدِقَاءَ.
Change to 'used to': أَلْعَبُ فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ. Then: أَقْرَأُ قِصَصًا.
Translate: 'My grandfather was a teacher.' and 'My sisters were shy.'
independent: Core: write five sentences about yourself at age six using كَانَ and at least two 'used to' sentences.
Extend: add the contrast with now (الْآنَ) and a reason with لِأَنَّ.
Stretch: add the negative لَمْ أَكُنْ أُحِبُّ الْخُضْرَوَاتِ and write a 60-word paragraph.
exit: Write the Arabic for 'my sister was shy' and 'we were friends'.
Translate: 'I used to live in a small town.'
lessons.homework: Write a 60-word paragraph in Arabic: what I was like when I was younger and what I used to do. Underline every كَانَ.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give a sentence frame (عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا، كُنْتُ ___ وَكُنْتُ أَ___) and the table on a card. Stretch: add كَانَتْ + passive-style detail or the negative لَمْ أَكُنْ.

lessons.unit: Unit 1.1: Who am I?
lessons.title: Role models and the people we admire
lessons.bigQuestion: What qualities make someone worth looking up to?
objectives: Describe a role model with five or more character adjectives
Give reasons using لِأَنَّ + pronoun ending
Join sentences with a relative clause (الَّذِي / الَّتِي)
successCriteria: All: say who your role model is and give one reason
Most: use at least four adjectives and مُعْجَبٌ بِ
Some: use الَّذِي / الَّتِي correctly in a longer answer
lessons.crossCurricular: History/RE: lives of admirable figures; PSHE: character and aspiration
lessons.smsc: Spiritual and moral: the Prophet ﷺ as the best example; virtues such as honesty and generosity
starter: Retrieval: give three past forms of كَانَ (I / she / we).
Translate: 'My friend was kind and funny.'
Say in Arabic: 'I used to play football every day.'

teach.heading: Character adjectives
teach.note: Introduce the vocabulary with gestures. Check feminine forms by adding ة. Ask pupils which of these qualities they value most and why. Note صَادِقٌ (honest) and كَرِيمٌ (generous) are also on many lists. Remind that a role model can be a family member, a teacher or a historical figure. Choral repetition then rapid translation.

teach.heading: Explaining my role model
bullets: أَنَا مُعْجَبٌ بِهَا (m) / أَنَا مُعْجَبَةٌ بِهَا (f)
anā muʿjabun bihā / anā muʿjabatun bihā
teach.note: Teach the frame: قُدْوَتِي + person + لِأَنَّ + pronoun ending + adjectives. The pronoun ending on لِأَنَّ must match the person: لِأَنَّهُ (he), لِأَنَّهَا (she). That is the key accuracy point. Do the adjective agreement: أُمِّي is feminine so the adjectives are feminine (صَبُورَةٌ). Practise with three famous people the class knows.

teach.heading: Higher: the relative clause

left.title: Masculine: الَّذِي
points: أَبِي هُوَ الشَّخْصُ الَّذِي يُسَاعِدُنِي دَائِمًا
abī huwa sh-shakhṣu lladhī yusāʿidunī dāʾiman
My father is the person who always helps me

right.title: Feminine: الَّتِي
points: أُمِّي هِيَ الْمَرْأَةُ الَّتِي تُسَاعِدُنِي دَائِمًا
ummī hiya l-marʾatu llatī tusāʿidunī dāʾiman
My mother is the woman who always helps me

teach.note: Present the relative pronouns: الَّذِي (m) and الَّتِي (f), used after a DEFINITE noun. Ask pupils to spot the definite noun (الشَّخْصُ, الْمَرْأَةُ). The pronoun refers back to the person: it is not 'who' in the question sense. Warn that after an indefinite noun no pronoun is used (taught in Year 11). This gives a Higher-tier structure for speaking and writing.

teach.heading: An authentic example

quote.text: لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِي رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ'You have in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example.'

teach.note: Only use this with care and respect. Surah al-Ahzab 33:21: the first clause is quoted. Ask pupils to annotate: which word means 'example' (أُسْوَةٌ) and which adjective means 'excellent' (حَسَنَةٌ). Teacher: check the vowelling against a mushaf before displaying. Link to the Qur'an and RE curriculum; the Arabic lesson is about reading and understanding the sentence structure (لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ = 'you have/there was for you').

teach.heading: Model: a developed answer

model.problem: Say: 'My role model is my grandfather. He is the man who taught me patience. I admire him because he is honest.'
steps: قُدْوَتِي جَدِّي
'the man who' = هُوَ الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي
'taught me patience' = عَلَّمَنِي الصَّبْرَ
'I admire him because he is honest' = أَنَا مُعْجَبٌ بِهِ لِأَنَّهُ صَادِقٌ
model.answer: قُدْوَتِي جَدِّي. هُوَ الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَنِي الصَّبْرَ. أَنَا مُعْجَبٌ بِهِ لِأَنَّهُ صَادِقٌ.

teach.note: Show how to move from one flat sentence to a developed one: add a reason, a relative clause and a second adjective. Pupils compare the 'basic' and 'developed' version and say which would score higher in the conversation. Then set pupils to write their own, changing the person and the qualities.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which completes: 'My teacher is my role model because she is patient'?
check.why: A woman needs لِأَنَّهَا and the feminine adjective صَبُورَةٌ. A uses he; C has the right pronoun but a masculine adjective; D says 'because I'.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. The trap is the pronoun ending on لِأَنَّ and the agreement of the adjective with a feminine person. If pupils choose A, they have used the masculine ending for a woman.

practice: Add the correct ending: قُدْوَتِي أَبِي لِأَنَّ___ شُجَاعٌ. / قُدْوَتِي أُخْتِي لِأَنَّ___ مُجْتَهِدَةٌ.
Join with الَّذِي or الَّتِي: (a) هِيَ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ ___ تُحِبُّ الطُّلَّابَ (b) هُوَ الْعَالِمُ ___ اكْتَشَفَ الدَّوَاءَ.
Say three sentences about a famous person you admire, giving a reason each time.
independent: Core: write 5 sentences about your role model using adjectives and لِأَنَّ.
Extend: add مُعْجَبٌ بِ and one relative clause.
Stretch: write 80 to 100 words comparing two role models, using a past and a present verb.
exit: Translate: 'My father is brave because he helps people.'
Write one sentence with الَّذِي or الَّتِي.
lessons.homework: Write 70 words in Arabic about your role model. Use at least four adjectives and one relative clause.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: provide the adjective table with pictures and the frame قُدْوَتِي ___ لِأَنَّ___ ___. Stretch: add a second reason with وَأَيْضًا and a contrast with وَلَكِنْ.

lessons.unit: Unit 1.1: Who am I?
lessons.title: Arabic in my life and in Arabic-speaking communities
lessons.bigQuestion: Why does studying Arabic open doors to different communities?
objectives: Name Arabic-speaking countries and nationalities
Say how long and why you study Arabic using مُنْذُ
Explain how study differs at home and in Arabic-speaking communities
successCriteria: All: name five countries and say you study Arabic
Most: use مُنْذُ + number and give two reasons
Some: compare studying in Britain with studying in an Arabic-speaking country
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: the Arab world; History: spread of the Arabic language
lessons.smsc: Social and cultural: respect for different communities; Spiritual: Arabic as the language of the Qur'an
starter: Retrieval: say three qualities of a role model in Arabic.
Translate: 'My mother is the woman who helps me.'
Write the Arabic for 'I studied', 'she studied', 'we studied' (verb دَرَسَ).

teach.heading: Countries and nationalities
teach.note: Show the map; pupils point. Nationality adjectives end in -ī (feminine -iyya). Ask pupils to give the feminine: مِصْرِيَّةٌ, سُعُودِيَّةٌ. Note that the exam uses Modern Standard Arabic, so the formal names are used, not dialect forms. Also mention that Arabic is spoken in over twenty countries. Links to Geography.

teach.heading: Why and for how long I study Arabic
bullets: I have studied Arabic for three years
لِأَنَّهَا لُغَةُ الْقُرْآنِ وَلِأَنَّ أَقَارِبِي يَتَكَلَّمُونَهَا
because it is the language of the Qur'an and my relatives speak it
teach.note: Key grammar: Arabic uses the PRESENT tense with مُنْذُ for 'have been doing' (أَدْرُسُ ... مُنْذُ), where English uses 'have studied'. Pupils often use the past tense: correct it. سَنَةٌ is feminine, so 'three years' is ثَلَاثُ سَنَوَاتٍ (the number has no -a ending with a feminine noun, and the noun is genitive plural). Elicit pupils' own reasons; be inclusive of those with Arabic-speaking and non-Arabic-speaking family.

teach.heading: Study at home and abroad

left.title: In Britain
points: I do not hear it much in the street

teach.note: Pupils compare their experience with what they know of schools in Arabic-speaking countries (formal Arabic is the language of textbooks, while people speak dialects at home). Emphasise: the exam tests formal Arabic; real communities mix both. Do not make claims about specific countries' timetables unless certain; use what pupils know or have read. Prompt pupils to produce a sentence on each side.

teach.heading: Model: a paragraph for the speaking exam

model.problem: Say: 'I am British. I have studied Arabic for four years because I want to speak with my grandmother. I would like to visit Egypt.'
steps: 'I am British' = أَنَا بَرِيطَانِيٌّ / بَرِيطَانِيَّةٌ
'for four years' = مُنْذُ أَرْبَعِ سَنَوَاتٍ (present verb: أَدْرُسُ)
'because I want to speak with' = لِأَنَّنِي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ مَعَ جَدَّتِي
'I would like to visit' = أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَزُورَ مِصْرَ
model.answer: أَنَا بَرِيطَانِيٌّ. أَدْرُسُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ مُنْذُ أَرْبَعِ سَنَوَاتٍ لِأَنَّنِي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ مَعَ جَدَّتِي. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَزُورَ مِصْرَ.

teach.note: Show the building blocks: from where? how long? why? what next? Ask pupils to count how many details are in the model. Stress that in the conversation each answer should be 2 to 3 sentences. Recycle the verb before the subject: أَنَا مِنْ ... Pupils translate the model back to English to check.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'I have studied Arabic for two years'?
check.why: Arabic uses the present tense with مُنْذُ for an action that began in the past and continues. 'Two years' is the dual سَنَتَيْنِ, not a number plus noun. A is the past tense, C has wrong number agreement, D is future.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. The trap in A is the English-style past tense; B and D change the meaning (duration vs completed action or the wrong number agreement).

practice: Give the nationality (m and f) for: مِصْرُ, الْمَغْرِبُ, الْعِرَاقُ.
Write: 'I have studied Arabic for five years.'
Say two reasons for studying Arabic using لِأَنَّ.
independent: Core: write 5 sentences about yourself and Arabic (nationality, how long, why).
Extend: add a sentence about a country you would like to visit and why.
Stretch: write a short comparison (60 words) of studying Arabic in Britain and in an Arabic-speaking country.
exit: Translate: 'My cousin is Jordanian. He speaks Arabic every day.'
Say how long you have studied Arabic and why.
lessons.homework: Prepare a 30-second spoken answer (record it) about why you study Arabic. Use مُنْذُ and لِأَنَّ.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give a country table with flags and a sentence frame. Stretch: add the dual and a contrast with بَيْنَمَا (whereas).

lessons.unit: Unit 1.2: Daily life
lessons.title: Shopping: clothes, prices and opinions
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I buy things and say what I think of them in Arabic?
objectives: Name clothes and shops; ask about prices
Use numbers with currency correctly
Weigh up shopping in shops and online
successCriteria: All: ask how much something costs and say it is cheap or expensive
Most: use numbers and currency correctly for 2, 5 and 20
Some: give advantages and disadvantages of online shopping
lessons.crossCurricular: Business Studies: prices and discounts; Maths: money
lessons.smsc: Moral: honesty and fairness in trade; avoiding waste (isrāf)
starter: Retrieval: write the Arabic numbers 5, 10, 20 and 100.
Say two things you like to eat and why.
Translate: 'The shop is big and cheap.'

teach.heading: Clothes and shopping words
teach.note: Show real or photo items. Teach by miming and swapping: 'is it big?' Note that حِذَاءٌ means 'a shoe/pair of shoes' and the plural is أَحْذِيَةٌ. Do not translate word for word. Pupils practise saying one item and one colour per turn.

teach.heading: Prices: numbers with currency
teach.note: The rule is the heart of this lesson: 1 and 2 follow the noun (singular or dual), 3 to 10 take the plural noun in the genitive, 11 to 99 take a singular noun in the accusative, 100 takes the singular genitive. Use جُنَيْهٌ (pound) as in Egypt; British pupils may say جُنَيْهٌ إِسْتِرْلِينِيٌّ. Drill with prices on the board. Common error: خَمْسَةُ جُنَيْهٌ.

teach.heading: In the shop
bullets: هُوَ غَالٍ جِدًّا. هَلْ يُوجَدُ خَصْمٌ؟
It is very expensive. Is there a discount?
teach.note: Role-play pairs: customer and shopkeeper. The customer asks the price, asks for a size and a colour, and decides. Keep exchanges at the exam level: 2 to 3 short turns. Focus on pronunciation of the question. In the role play the exam expects a polite tone (مِنْ فَضْلِكَ, شُكْرًا).

teach.heading: Model: asking the price

model.problem: Say: 'How much is this bag?' (answer: twenty pounds) then 'It is expensive. Is there a discount?'
steps: 'How much is this bag?' = بِكَمْ هَذِهِ الْحَقِيبَةُ؟
Answer: عِشْرُونَ جُنَيْهًا
'It is expensive' (feminine agreement) = هِيَ غَالِيَةٌ
'Is there a discount?' = هَلْ يُوجَدُ خَصْمٌ؟
model.answer: بِكَمْ هَذِهِ الْحَقِيبَةُ؟ - عِشْرُونَ جُنَيْهًا. - هِيَ غَالِيَةٌ. هَلْ يُوجَدُ خَصْمٌ؟

teach.note: Think aloud: the feminine demonstrative هَذِهِ goes with حَقِيبَةٌ (feminine), and the adjective is feminine too (غَالِيَةٌ). Then use the number rule for 20. Pupils swap the item for a shirt (masculine: هَذَا الْقَمِيصُ ... غَالٍ) to check they can change the agreement.

teach.heading: Online or in the shop?

left.title: Online shopping
points: I cannot try the clothes on

teach.note: Ask pupils to say which column each idea belongs to. Then pupils add their own idea. This supports the 'advantages and disadvantages' task in Theme 1 (also developed in the technology lesson). Note the structure: مِنْ مَزَايَا ... (one of the advantages) and مِنْ عُيُوبِ ... (one of the disadvantages).

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.why: 11 to 99 take a singular accusative noun: عِشْرُونَ جُنَيْهًا. A uses the plural (3 to 10 rule); C is the genitive (100 rule); D is the dual.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. The distractors reflect the three number rules: plural, singular accusative, singular genitive. If pupils choose C, they have used the 'three to ten' rule for 20.

practice: Ask the price of: a bag, a dress, a pair of shoes. Answer with 5, 20 and 100 pounds.
Write the dual and a number phrase: 'two shirts', 'five shirts'.
Role play: ask for a size and say you find it expensive.
independent: Core: write a shop dialogue of 6 lines using بِكَمْ, a size and a price.
Extend: add a discount negotiation.
Stretch: write 80 words: online or in the shop? Give two advantages and two disadvantages.
exit: Write in Arabic: 'How much is this bag?' 'It is twenty pounds.'
Give one advantage of online shopping.
lessons.homework: Write a dialogue (8 lines) buying a gift for a friend. Use two prices.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the price-number table as a card. Stretch: add a comparative (أَرْخَصُ مِنْ) and a polite request with هَلْ يُمْكِنُ؟

lessons.unit: Unit 1.3: Cultural life
lessons.title: Reading, film, television and media
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I give and justify opinions about what I read, hear and watch?
objectives: Name types of books, programmes and media
Give opinions with يُعْجِبُنِي and adjectives
Review a film or book in the past tense
successCriteria: All: say what you like to read, listen to or watch
Most: give a reason and use two adjectives
Some: write a short review in the past tense with an opinion and a recommendation
lessons.crossCurricular: English: reviews and reading for pleasure; Islamic Studies: choosing beneficial media
lessons.smsc: Social and cultural: choosing suitable media with adab; critical thinking
starter: Retrieval: say what you did yesterday in the past tense (two verbs).
Write the Arabic for 'I like football because it is fun'.
Say the Arabic for 'cheap' and 'expensive'.

teach.heading: Books, film, TV and media
teach.note: Start with the pupils' own choices. Match verbs to nouns: أَقْرَأُ (read), أَسْتَمِعُ إِلَى (listen to), أُشَاهِدُ (watch). Common mistake: using أَسْمَعُ for deliberate listening: use أَسْتَمِعُ إِلَى plus a noun. Sport is covered in the Y10 free-time lesson, so refer back to it for the sport sub-topic. Exam vocabulary to recognise only: أُغْنِيَةٌ (song) and مُوسِيقَى (music) can appear in listening and reading texts, so pupils should understand them; pupils give their own opinions about books, documentaries and programmes.

teach.heading: Opinions and reasons
bullets: يُعْجِبُنِي هَذَا الْمُسَلْسَلُ لِأَنَّ قِصَّتَهُ مُمْتِعَةٌ
yuʿjibunī hādhā l-musalsalu li-anna qiṣṣatahu mumtiʿatun
I like this series because its story is enjoyable
I do not like the film because it is boring
teach.note: Teach that the thing liked is the subject of يُعْجِبُنِي (so it follows the verb and is nominative). Pupils often say أَنَا يُعْجِبُنِي: drill the correct word order. Negation with لَا before a present verb. Give reasons with لِأَنَّ + noun with the pronoun ending (قِصَّتَهُ = its story). Opinion adjectives: مُمْتِعٌ, مُمِلٌّ, مُفِيدٌ (useful), مُضْحِكٌ.

teach.heading: Reviewing in the past

model.problem: Write a two-sentence review: 'Yesterday I watched a documentary about Egypt. It was very enjoyable and I recommend it.'
steps: 'Yesterday I watched' = أَمْسِ شَاهَدْتُ
'a documentary about Egypt' = بَرْنَامَجًا وَثَائِقِيًّا عَنْ مِصْرَ
'It was very enjoyable' = كَانَ مُمْتِعًا جِدًّا
'I recommend it' = وَأَنْصَحُ بِمُشَاهَدَتِهِ
model.answer: أَمْسِ شَاهَدْتُ بَرْنَامَجًا وَثَائِقِيًّا عَنْ مِصْرَ. كَانَ مُمْتِعًا جِدًّا وَأَنْصَحُ بِمُشَاهَدَتِهِ.

teach.note: Model a short review with a past verb for what happened and كَانَ for description. Then add a recommendation: أَنْصَحُ بِمُشَاهَدَتِهِ (I recommend watching it). Pupils underline each past verb and each كَانَ in the model.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.why: قِصَّةٌ is feminine, so the verb is تُعْجِبُنِي and the story is the subject. A and C add an unwanted أَنَا; D has a masculine verb and the wrong case.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. If pupils choose C, they have placed أَنَا before يُعْجِبُنِي, which gives 'I please me'. Re-teach: the thing that pleases is the subject.

practice: Match the verb: أَقْرَأُ / أَسْتَمِعُ إِلَى / أُشَاهِدُ with رِوَايَةً, تِلَاوَةً, فِيلْمًا.
Say what you think of a series you have seen, with a reason.
Translate: 'The film was boring but the documentary was useful.'
independent: Core: write 5 opinion sentences with يُعْجِبُنِي / لَا يُعْجِبُنِي and لِأَنَّ.
Extend: add a past review of one film or book.
Stretch: write 80 words recommending one thing to read, hear or watch, and why a friend should enjoy it.
exit: Write: 'I like this novel because the story is exciting.'
Say one thing you do not like and why.
lessons.homework: Write a 6-sentence review of a book, film or programme you know. Use at least one past verb and one opinion adjective.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the opinion frame with the adjective bank. Stretch: add the contrast أَمَّا ... فَ... (as for ... then ...) and a recommendation.

lessons.title: Holidays: preferences, destinations and past experiences
lessons.bigQuestion: What makes a holiday meaningful, not just fun?
objectives: To understand how to talk about holiday preferences and describe a past holiday, including 'Umrah or visiting family
successCriteria: All: say where I like to go and why
Most: describe a past holiday with the past tense and كَانَ
Some: link past, present and future in one answer
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: 'Umrah as a journey of worship

hook.text: What makes a holiday meaningful, not just fun?
hook.a: Spending time with family, learning, worship such as 'Umrah, and helping others.

teach.heading: Preferences
bullets: لَا أُحِبُّ العُطَلَ فِي المُدُنِ الكَبِيرَةِ
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: A past holiday
teach.note: Our own model.

quote.text:
فِي الصَّيْفِ المَاضِي سَافَرْتُ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي إِلَى مَكَّةَ لِأَدَاءِ العُمْرَةِ.
نَزَلْنَا فِي فُنْدُقٍ قَرِيبٍ مِنَ الحَرَمِ، وَكَانَ الطَّقْسُ حَارًّا جِدًّا.
بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ زُرْنَا أَقَارِبَنَا فِي جُدَّةَ.
فِي المُسْتَقْبَلِ سَأَزُورُ المَدِينَةَ المُنَوَّرَةَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ.

teach.heading: Three time frames
teach.note: The examiner rewards range.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: نَزَلْنَا فِي فُنْدُقٍ قَرِيبٍ مِنَ الحَرَمِ.

practice.q: Say: last year I visited my relatives in Pakistan.
practice.a: فِي السَّنَةِ المَاضِيَةِ زُرْتُ أَقَارِبِي فِي بَاكِسْتَان
practice.model: Teacher: time phrase (فِي السَّنَةِ المَاضِيَةِ) + past verb (زُرْتُ) + object (أَقَارِبِي) + place.

practice.q: وِجْهَة means ...

independent.q: Exam-style writing (our own) in the portal response box, 100 words: 'صِفْ عُطْلَةً قُمْتَ بِهَا، وَأَيْنَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ فِي المُسْتَقْبَلِ.' Use three time frames and two opinions.
independent.a: Three time frames, opinions with reasons, accurate past tense
independent.model: Teacher shows a plan with the three time frames from the timeline slide.

independent.a: Group A: accurate summary and i'rab; Group B: fluent spoken answer

exit.q: عُمْرَة is ...
Back to our ponder: what makes a holiday meaningful?
exit.a: Family, learning, worship and helping others.

lessons.unit: Unit 2.1: Holidays
lessons.title: Holiday experiences: telling the story
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I describe what happened on holiday in order?
objectives: Use common past-tense verbs including 'hollow' verbs
Sequence events using أَوَّلًا ثُمَّ ...
Give opinions about a holiday in the past
successCriteria: All: say where you went and what you did with 3 past verbs
Most: conjugate hollow verbs such as زَارَ in I and we forms
Some: write a 90-word holiday recount with sequencing and opinions
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: places; English: narrative writing
lessons.smsc: Moral and cultural: gratitude for blessings and the chance to travel
starter: Retrieval: conjugate كَانَ for أَنَا, هِيَ, نَحْنُ.
Say: 'Next summer we will travel to Egypt.'
Name three holiday types in Arabic.

teach.heading: Past verbs for holidays
teach.note: Pupils know regular verbs. Today add useful irregular ones. Group the verbs: the regular (ذَهَبَ, سَافَرَ, أَكَلَ, سَبَحَ) and the 'hollow' verbs with a long vowel in the middle (زَارَ, نَامَ) and the 'defective' ones that end in a vowel (اِشْتَرَى, رَأَى). Say: for hollow verbs the long vowel is dropped before the -tu / -nā endings. Choral drill the I and we forms.

teach.heading: Careful with hollow verbs

misconception.right: زُرْتُ الْمَتْحَفَ / نِمْنَا مُتَأَخِّرِينَ - the long vowel disappears and the first letter takes a short vowel

teach.note: Show the typical error and the correction, and explain why. Elicit the 'rule' from pupils rather than giving it: what happens to the alif? Transliteration: zurtu (not zārtu), nimtu (not nāmtu). Make pupils write five hollow forms on whiteboards (قَالَ → قُلْتُ).

teach.heading: Telling the story in order
bullets: ثُمَّ نَزَلْنَا فِي فُنْدُقٍ قَرِيبٍ مِنَ الْبَحْرِ
Then we stayed in a hotel near the sea
After that we visited the museum
In the end the holiday was wonderful
teach.note: Explain that sequencing words make a text feel connected, and that examiners reward them. Pupils underline the four sequencing words. Note that فُنْدُقٌ takes tanween because it is indefinite and in the genitive after فِي. Use كَانَتْ with الْعُطْلَةُ (feminine). Pupils then retell their own holiday as a 4-sentence chain.

teach.heading: Model: a holiday recount

model.problem: Translate: 'Last summer we travelled to Turkey. We stayed in a hotel near the sea and the weather was hot. I swam every day.'
steps: 'Last summer we travelled to Turkey' = الصَّيْفَ الْمَاضِيَ سَافَرْنَا إِلَى تُرْكِيَا
'we stayed in a hotel near the sea' = نَزَلْنَا فِي فُنْدُقٍ قَرِيبٍ مِنَ الْبَحْرِ
'and the weather was hot' = وَكَانَ الْجَوُّ حَارًّا
'I swam every day' = سَبَحْتُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ
model.answer: الصَّيْفَ الْمَاضِيَ سَافَرْنَا إِلَى تُرْكِيَا. نَزَلْنَا فِي فُنْدُقٍ قَرِيبٍ مِنَ الْبَحْرِ وَكَانَ الْجَوُّ حَارًّا. سَبَحْتُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.

teach.note: Think aloud, pointing out the three-part structure: where and when, what we did, how it was. Highlight the verb forms: سَافَرْنَا, نَزَلْنَا, سَبَحْتُ. Pupils translate back into English orally to check meaning.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.why: Hollow verbs shorten the vowel before -nā: زُرْنَا. B keeps the long alif, C has the wrong short vowel, D means 'he visited'.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A and C show unadjusted hollow stems; D is the 'he' form. Ask pupils which letter is missing in the right answer.

practice: Give the I and we forms of: ذَهَبَ, نَامَ, اِشْتَرَى.
Put in order and translate: ثُمَّ / أَوَّلًا / وَفِي النِّهَايَةِ with three events you choose.
Translate: 'The hotel was very good and the food was delicious.'
independent: Core: write 5 past-tense sentences about a real or imagined holiday.
Extend: add sequencing words and two opinion sentences.
Stretch: write 90 words including a problem on the holiday and how it was solved.
exit: Write: 'I saw the sea and swam.'
Write: 'We slept late and then visited a museum.'
lessons.homework: Write a 90-word recount of a holiday (real or imagined). Include four different past verbs and two sequencing words.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the verb table and sequencing words on a card; allow a 5-sentence version. Stretch: add habits with كَانَ + present (كُنْتُ أَسْبَحُ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ) and a contrast with وَلَكِنْ.

hook.text: What makes a good place to stay on holiday?

teach.heading: Accommodation
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Booking
teach.note: Our own role play.

quote.text:
- أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَحْجِزَ غُرْفَةً لِشَخْصَيْنِ لِثَلَاثِ لَيَالٍ.
- هَلْ تُرِيدُ إِطْلَالَةً عَلَى البَحْرِ؟
- نَعَمْ، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. كَمِ السِّعْرُ؟
- مِئَةُ جُنَيْهٍ فِي اللَّيْلَةِ، مَعَ الفُطُورِ.

teach.heading: Three time frames
bullets: Past: نَزَلْتُ فِي فُنْدُقٍ قَرِيبٍ مِنَ الحَرَمِ

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: لِثَلَاثِ لَيَالٍ: three nights.

practice.q: Say: I want to book a room for one person for two nights.
practice.a: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَحْجِزَ غُرْفَةً لِشَخْصٍ وَاحِدٍ لِلَيْلَتَيْنِ
practice.model: Teacher: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَحْجِزَ + غُرْفَةً + لِشَخْصٍ وَاحِدٍ + لِلَيْلَتَيْنِ (dual).

practice.q: إِطْلَالَة means ...

independent.q: Extend: Group A (4AA1): write a three-sentence summary of your answer in other words and give the i'rab of one sentence. Group B (1AA0): say your answer aloud in a breakout and answer one follow-up question.
independent.a: Group A: accurate summary and i'rab; Group B: fluent spoken answer

exit.q: حَجْز means ...
Back to our ponder: what makes a good place to stay?
exit.a: Clean, safe, near a masjid, good service.

lessons.title: Asking for help and dealing with problems
lessons.bigQuestion: When something goes wrong on a journey, what helps most: patience, politeness or knowing the language?

successCriteria: All: ask for help with مِنْ فَضْلِكَ
Most: explain a problem (lost, late, broken)
Some: suggest a solution and respond in a role play

hook.text: When something goes wrong on a journey, what helps most: patience, politeness or knowing the language?
hook.a: All three; patience is a virtue and politeness opens doors.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah is kind and loves kindness in all matters' (Bukhari and Muslim): politeness when things go wrong.

starter.q: Say 'next year I will visit Madinah'.

teach.heading: Problems
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Asking politely
bullets: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، هَلْ يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تُسَاعِدَنِي؟

teach.heading: Role play
teach.note: Our own, 1AA0 style.

- مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، عِنْدِي مُشْكِلَةٌ فِي غُرْفَتِي.

practice.q: Explain: I lost my bag at the station; can you help me?

lessons.unit: Unit 2.3: Town, region and country
lessons.title: Weather, seasons and comparing places
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I describe and compare the weather in different places?
objectives: Describe weather and seasons
Form and use comparatives with أَفْعَلُ ... مِنْ
Give a simple weather forecast in the future
successCriteria: All: describe today's weather with 3 words
Most: compare two places with a comparative and مِنْ
Some: write a forecast and a comparison paragraph
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: climate and weather; Science: temperature
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: reflecting on the signs of Allah's creation in the seasons and weather
starter: Bismillah. Retrieval: say 'We stayed in a hotel near the sea'.
Say the past of 'to see' for 'I'.
Name three types of holiday in Arabic.

teach.heading: Weather words
teach.note: Begin with the question كَيْفَ الْجَوُّ الْيَوْمَ؟ (How is the weather today?) and answer by looking out of the window or at a screen. The adjectives agree with الْجَوُّ (masculine). حَارٌّ has a shadda: the double -r. For snow use the verb يَسْقُطُ الثَّلْجُ (snow falls). Link the seasons: الصَّيْفُ, الشِّتَاءُ, الرَّبِيعُ, الْخَرِيفُ. Pupils note the weather for each season in Britain.

teach.heading: Comparatives
teach.note: The comparative pattern is أَفْعَلُ (a-f-ʿ-a-l). Pupils see the root letters in the new pattern: big كَبِير → أَكْبَرُ. These words are diptote: they never take tanween. 'Than' = مِنْ + the thing compared. Warn about double-letter adjectives: حَارٌّ becomes أَحَرُّ (one r). Pupils make five comparisons about the class. This is core for the writing paper and for the translation task.

teach.heading: Model: comparing and forecasting

model.problem: Say: 'Winter in Britain is colder than winter in Egypt. Tomorrow the weather will be sunny.'
steps: 'Winter in Britain' = الشِّتَاءُ فِي بَرِيطَانِيَا
'is colder than' = أَبْرَدُ مِنْ
'winter in Egypt' = الشِّتَاءِ فِي مِصْرَ (genitive after مِنْ)
'Tomorrow the weather will be sunny' = غَدًا سَيَكُونُ الْجَوُّ مُشْمِسًا
model.answer: الشِّتَاءُ فِي بَرِيطَانِيَا أَبْرَدُ مِنَ الشِّتَاءِ فِي مِصْرَ. غَدًا سَيَكُونُ الْجَوُّ مُشْمِسًا.

teach.note: Show the structure: A + comparative + مِنْ + B. Then the forecast: غَدًا + سَيَكُونُ. Pupils write their own with a different pair of places. Mention the superlative: أَجْمَلُ مَدِينَةٍ (the most beautiful city), which uses the comparative before an indefinite singular noun.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'The weather will be rainy tomorrow'?
check.why: غَدًا (tomorrow) and سَيَكُونُ (will be) mark the future. A is past, B is present, D compares seasons.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. B has the past tense; C has the present; D is a comparison, not a forecast. Ask which word marks the future.

practice: Describe the weather in two cities (your choice) today.
Make comparisons: بَرِيطَانِيَا / مِصْرُ with الصَّيْفُ; لَنْدَنُ / الْقَاهِرَةُ with كَبِيرَةٌ.
Translate: 'The weather was cold yesterday but tomorrow it will be warm.' (warm = دَافِئٌ)
independent: Core: write 5 weather sentences (one per season) about Britain.
Extend: add two comparisons with another country.
Stretch: write 90 words comparing two regions and explaining which you prefer.
exit: Write: 'Summer in Egypt is hotter than summer in Britain.'
Write a forecast for tomorrow in one sentence.
lessons.homework: Write a 5-day forecast (5 sentences) for a place of your choice using the future tense and at least two comparisons.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the weather table with symbols and the comparative table. Stretch: use the superlative (أَجْمَلُ فَصْلٍ) with a reason.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Local area, holiday and travel: town, region and country; holidays (2.3, 2.1)
lessons.title: My town: places to see and things to do
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I tell a visitor what there is, what there is not and what they can do?
objectives: To understand how to say what there is and is not in a town and suggest activities with يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ
successCriteria: All: say يُوجَدُ / فِيهَا and لَا يُوجَدُ
Most: suggest three activities with يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ + verb
Some: use the subjunctive ending correctly after أَنْ
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: services and amenities in settlements
lessons.smsc: Social: welcoming visitors and showing them the good in our area

hook.text: Your town has a tourism website in Arabic. What three places would you put on its front page?
hook.a: The masjid, a park, a museum or market; any with reasons.

islamicLink.text: Honouring a guest is part of faith; the Prophet ﷺ linked believing in Allah and the Last Day with honouring one's guest (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). Helping visitors enjoy our town is part of that.

starter.q: Say 'my town is in the north of England'.

teach.heading: There is, there is not

head: Arabic
English
rows: there is a museum in my town
it does not have an airport

teach.note: Begin with bismillah. فِيهَا (in it) refers back to مَدِينَة.

teach.heading: Places to see
bullets: مَعَالِمُ مَدِينَتِي: the sights of my town
teach.note: Pupils name real places in their own towns.

teach.heading: You can ...

model.problem: Suggest three things to do.
steps: يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَزُورَ المَسْجِدَ الكَبِيرَ
يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَتَجَوَّلَ فِي السُّوقِ
يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَقْرَأَ فِي المَكْتَبَةِ
model.answer: After أَنْ the verb ends in fathah: تَزُورَ، تَتَجَوَّلَ، تَقْرَأَ

teach.note: Group A: أَنْ is a حَرْفُ نَصْبٍ: the verb is مَنْصُوب. To a female: يُمْكِنُكِ أَنْ تَزُورِي (the ن drops).

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: After أَنْ the present verb takes fathah: تَزُورَ.

practice.q: Say: There is a big park in my town, but there is no cinema.
practice.a: يُوجَدُ فِي مَدِينَتِي حَدِيقَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ، لٰكِنْ لَا يُوجَدُ فِيهَا سِينَمَا.
practice.model:
يُوجَدُ فِي مَدِينَتِي + the place.
لٰكِنْ (but).
لَا يُوجَدُ فِيهَا + the missing place.

practice.q: Suggest to a female visitor: you can visit the museum.
What is قَلْعَة?

independent.q: Core: Write a 90-word guide for an Arabic-speaking visitor (portal response box): what there is, what there is not, three suggestions with يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ, and your favourite place with a reason.
independent.a: Marked for يُوجَدُ / لَا يُوجَدُ, subjunctive after أَنْ, places, opinion with reason.
independent.model: Teacher writes the opening: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا فِي مَدِينَتِي ... and one suggestion.

independent.q: Extend (Group B): prepare the role play line: 'Excuse me, what is there to do here?' and two answers.
independent.a: عَفْوًا، مَاذَا يُمْكِنُ أَنْ أَفْعَلَ هُنَا؟ يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَزُورَ ... / يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَتَسَوَّقَ ...

independent.q: Stretch (Group A): give the i'rab of تَزُورَ in يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَزُورَ.
independent.a: فِعْلٌ مُضَارِعٌ مَنْصُوبٌ بِأَنْ وَعَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ الفَتْحَةُ

exit.q: 'There is not': A) لَا يُوجَدُ B) يُوجَدُ C) يُمْكِنُ
Big question: suggest one thing a visitor can do in your town.
exit.a: For example: يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَزُورَ المَسْجِدَ الكَبِيرَ.

lessons.homework: Turn your guide into a short leaflet (text only or with photos of buildings and places, no people).
lessons.send: SEND: guide frame and place bank. EAL: picture cards of places. Stretch: يَجِبُ أَنْ تَزُورَ (you must visit) and لَا تَنْسَ أَنْ (do not forget to).
