lessons.unit: Unit 2.3: Town, region and country
lessons.title: Speaking skills: the picture-based task
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I turn a picture into a developed spoken answer?
objectives: Describe a picture using position phrases
Add opinions, past and future to extend an answer
Use أَنَّ correctly after أَعْتَقِدُ
successCriteria: All: describe who and where in the picture with 3 sentences
Most: add an opinion and a time reference
Some: develop answers to questions linked to the picture with reasons
lessons.crossCurricular: Art: describing images; English: oral presentation
lessons.smsc: Social: respectful communication; confidence in speaking
starter: Retrieval: say two things there are and one thing there is not in your town.
Give two comparatives.
Say 'next summer I will travel to Jordan'.

teach.heading: A language bank for pictures

head: Arabic
Transliteration
English
rows: on the right / on the left

teach.note: Hand out the bank. The speaking paper includes a picture-based task (24 marks, per the spec file); check the SAMs for how the questions are asked and the preparation time. The picture task rewards: accurate description, answers developed beyond one sentence, and a range of tenses. Practise by pairs describing a photo for 30 seconds without stopping.

teach.heading: Basic or developed?

left.title: Basic
points: فِي الصُّورَةِ عَائِلَةٌ. هُمْ عَلَى الشَّاطِئِ.
In the picture is a family. They are on the beach.

right.title: Developed
points: فِي الصُّورَةِ أَرَى عَائِلَةً عَلَى الشَّاطِئِ. عَلَى الْيَسَارِ يَلْعَبُ الْأَطْفَالُ بِالرَّمْلِ. أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ الْجَوَّ حَارٌّ.
I see a family on the beach. On the left the children play with the sand. I think the weather is hot.

teach.note: Show the two answers and ask which would gain more marks, and why: the right one has position, activity, opinion and a time reference. Ask pupils to count the extra pieces of information. Then they upgrade the left answer in pairs.

teach.heading: Watch the case after أَنَّ

misconception.right: أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ الْجَوَّ حَارٌّ - the subject after أَنَّ takes the accusative (-a)

teach.note: A very common error: after أَنَّ (and إِنَّ) the subject takes the accusative: الْجَوَّ. Pupils drill with five sentences using the same pattern. Mention that the pronoun suffix does the same: أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّهُ مُمْتِعٌ.

teach.heading: Model: a full picture description

model.problem: Describe a picture of a family on a beach, including an opinion and a link to a past holiday.
steps: Say what you see: فِي الصُّورَةِ أَرَى عَائِلَةً عَلَى الشَّاطِئِ
Describe positions and actions: عَلَى الْيَمِينِ يَجْلِسُ الْأَبُ وَالْأُمُّ تَحْتَ مِظَلَّةٍ، وَعَلَى الْيَسَارِ يَلْعَبُ الْأَطْفَالُ بِالرَّمْلِ
Add an opinion: أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ الْجَوَّ حَارٌّ وَمُشْمِسٌ، وَفِي رَأْيِي هَذِهِ عُطْلَةٌ مُمْتِعَةٌ
Link to the past: الصَّيْفَ الْمَاضِيَ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْبَحْرِ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي
model.answer: فِي الصُّورَةِ أَرَى عَائِلَةً عَلَى الشَّاطِئِ. عَلَى الْيَمِينِ يَجْلِسُ الْأَبُ وَالْأُمُّ تَحْتَ مِظَلَّةٍ، وَعَلَى الْيَسَارِ يَلْعَبُ الْأَطْفَالُ بِالرَّمْلِ. أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ الْجَوَّ حَارٌّ وَمُشْمِسٌ. فِي رَأْيِي هَذِهِ عُطْلَةٌ مُمْتِعَةٌ. الصَّيْفَ الْمَاضِيَ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الْبَحْرِ مَعَ عَائِلَتِي.

teach.note: Play it aloud as if in the exam. Count the pieces of information: place, position, activity, opinion, link to the past. The final past-tense sentence shows how to connect the picture to personal experience, which examiners reward. Pupils then practise with a different picture of their choice.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which phrase tells you something is on the LEFT of the picture?
check.why: عَلَى الْيَسَارِ means on the left. The others mean right, background and middle.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Distractors name other positions. Ask pupils to say the opposite phrase too.

practice: In pairs describe a photo of a street scene in 30 seconds: use three position phrases.
Add an opinion and a past sentence to your description.
Find and correct the case error: أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ الْمَطَرُ شَدِيدٌ.
independent: Core: prepare a 6-sentence description of a picture of a market.
Extend: add two answers to questions: 'Would you like to go there? Why?'
Stretch: record a 90-second answer with description, opinion, past and future.
exit: Write: 'On the right there are two boys. They are playing.'
Write: 'I think that the weather is cold.'
lessons.homework: Record a 60-second description of a photo from your phone or the school resources, with at least two position phrases and one opinion.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give the language bank and sentence starters; allow a written plan. Stretch: add the unreal 'if I were there' with لَوْ كُنْتُ هُنَاكَ.

lessons.unit: Unit 2.3: Town, region and country
lessons.title: Reading skills: roots, patterns and unknown words
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I work out a word I have never met?
objectives: Identify three-letter roots
Use patterns to guess meaning
Apply skimming, scanning and decoding to a short text
successCriteria: All: find the root of a word
Most: guess meaning from root and context
Some: answer questions on a short advert with accurate English
lessons.crossCurricular: English: reading strategies and vocabulary; Linguistics: Semitic roots
lessons.smsc: Spiritual and cultural: appreciating the structure of the Arabic language and its link to Qur'an reading
starter: Retrieval: describe a picture: say two position phrases.
Say the Arabic for 'there is no stadium in my town'.
Give the comparative of كَبِيرٌ and بَارِدٌ.

teach.heading: One root, many words
teach.note: Reveal the root letters in colour (ك ت ب) and ask what the words share. This shows pupils that Arabic vocabulary is built, so knowing a root multiplies vocabulary. Warn: root meaning is a guide, not a guarantee; check against context. Pupils choose another root and find three words in their book or the vocabulary lists.

teach.heading: Reading strategy
bullets: Skim: title, first line, numbers, names
Scan: find the word the question asks for
Check: does your English answer make sense?
teach.note: Teach the four-step method. Emphasise reading the question FIRST, then the text. In Paper 3 pupils may not use dictionaries, so decoding unknown words is essential. Loanwords (تِلِفِزْيُون, إِنْتَرْنِت, بَنْك) are free marks. Also stress: do not leave blanks; make an informed guess from context. In the translation section be accurate and do not omit small words.

teach.heading: A practice text

quote.text: فُنْدُقُ النِّيلِ يَدْعُوكُمْ لِقَضَاءِ عُطْلَتِكُمْ فِي مَدِينَةِ أَسْوَانَ. غُرَفٌ وَاسِعَةٌ تُطِلُّ عَلَى النِّيلِ، وَمَطْعَمٌ يُقَدِّمُ الْأَكْلَاتِ الشَّرْقِيَّةَ، وَحَمَّامُ سِبَاحَةٍ لِلْكِبَارِ وَالصِّغَارِ. الْأَسْعَارُ تَبْدَأُ مِنْ مِئَتَيْ جُنَيْهٍ لِلَّيْلَةِ.
quote.source: Original practice text for this lesson (Nile Hotel advert)

teach.note: Read aloud, then silently. Pupils underline every word whose root they can identify. They then decide: what kind of text is this (advert) and who is it for (visitors)? Translation of key parts is on the model slide. This is an original practice text written for this lesson, not an exam extract.

teach.heading: Model: decoding an unknown word

model.problem: Work out the meaning of يَدْعُوكُمْ in 'Nile Hotel يَدْعُوكُمْ لِقَضَاءِ عُطْلَتِكُمْ'.
steps: Find the root: د ع و
Think of related words you know: دَعْوَةٌ (invitation), دُعَاءٌ (du'a)
Note the ending كُمْ = 'you' (plural) and يَـ = he/it does
Test it in the context of an advert: 'invites you to spend your holiday'
model.answer: يَدْعُوكُمْ = 'invites you (plural)'. The sentence: The Nile Hotel invites you to spend your holiday in Aswan.

teach.note: Think aloud. The pupil does not know يَدْعُوكُمْ, so: look for the root (د ع و), think of دُعَاءٌ (supplication) and دَعْوَةٌ (invitation): the verb means 'invites'. Context (an advert, 'to spend your holiday') confirms it. Stress the habit: root, pattern, context, then check the whole sentence.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: What is the root of مَدْرَسَةٌ (school)?
check.why: The root is د ر س (to study); the initial م and final ة are added by the pattern. مَدْرَسَةٌ is 'a place of studying'.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. The roots of the options differ by one letter; ask pupils to find the three consonants in order, ignoring prefixes (م) and endings (ة).

practice: Find the root of: مُسَافِرٌ, مَكْتَبَةٌ, زِيَارَةٌ.
Read the practice text. Answer in English: (a) Where is the hotel? (b) What does the room overlook? (c) What is the lowest price?
Underline three words you can understand from their roots.
independent: Core: answer 5 questions in English on the Nile Hotel advert.
Extend: translate the last sentence into English accurately.
Stretch: write a similar advert (50 words) for a hotel in Britain, in Arabic.
exit: What is the root of مُدَرِّسٌ?
What does 'مِئَتَيْ جُنَيْهٍ' mean?
lessons.homework: Find five new words from the root س ف ر or د ر س in a dictionary or the vocabulary list. Write each with its meaning and use it in a sentence.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give a glossary of 5 words and the root table. Stretch: add a text with unfamiliar vocabulary and no glossary.

lessons.title: Relationships: getting on with family, then and now
lessons.bigQuestion: How have my relationships with my family changed since I was younger?
objectives: Describe relationships with family members
Contrast how things were when younger with how they are now
Use كُنْتُ + present verb for what I used to do
successCriteria: All: say two things about a family relationship
Most: say what you used to do and what you do now
Some: explain why a relationship has changed using لِأَنَّ

keywords.def: when I was little (ʿindamā kuntu ṣaghīran)

starter: Retrieval: say two adjectives describing your best friend in Arabic.
Retrieval: say 'my mother is kind' in Arabic.
Retrieval: say 'yesterday I played football' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Family relationships

head: Arabic
Transliteration
English
rows: my relationship with my mother is strong
I get on well with my father
I sometimes argue with my brother
I respect my grandfather and grandmother

teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Introduce the four patterns and ask pupils to say which is true for them. Note that مَعَ is followed by the genitive (أَبِي, أَخِي). Link to birr al-wālidayn: kindness to parents is a major theme of the Qur'an (for example 17:23, verify reference before quoting).

teach.heading: When I was younger

left.title: Then (كُنْتُ + verb)
points: كُنْتُ أَلْعَبُ مَعَ جَدَّتِي - I used to play with my grandmother
كُنْتُ أَتَشَاجَرُ مَعَ أَخِي - I used to argue with my brother

right.title: Now (present)
points: أَنَا أَكْثَرُ هُدُوءًا - I am calmer
أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي - I visit my grandmother

teach.note: Habitual past = كَانَ in the past + present-tense verb. Girls say كُنْتُ خَجُولَةً. Pupils may already know kāna from the earlier past-tense lesson, so keep this as retrieval and build the contrast. Ask: which verb carries the past meaning? (كُنْتُ). Which carries the action? (أَلْعَبُ).

teach.heading: Model: then and now

model.problem: Translate: 'When I was younger I was shy and I used to play with my cousin every day. Now I get on well with my parents.'
steps: 'When I was younger' = عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا
'I was shy' = كُنْتُ خَجُولًا
'I used to play with my cousin' = كُنْتُ أَلْعَبُ مَعَ ابْنِ عَمِّي
'every day' = كُلَّ يَوْمٍ
'Now I get on well with my parents' = الْآنَ أَتَفَاهَمُ جَيِّدًا مَعَ وَالِدَيَّ
model.answer: عِنْدَمَا كُنْتُ صَغِيرًا، كُنْتُ خَجُولًا وَكُنْتُ أَلْعَبُ مَعَ ابْنِ عَمِّي كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. الْآنَ أَتَفَاهَمُ جَيِّدًا مَعَ وَالِدَيَّ.

teach.note: Think aloud: find the time marker first, then choose the tense. Point out وَالِدَيَّ (my parents) after مَعَ: the dual genitive ending with ياء. Ask for other cousin words (ابْنَةُ خَالَتِي and so on) but keep to what pupils have met. Arabic specialist to check the cousin terms.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which sentence means 'I used to play with my brother'?
check.why: كُنْتُ + present verb gives 'used to'. B is 'I play', C is 'I will play', D has the wrong subject (my brother used to play with me).

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. If pupils choose D, ask who the subject is (the verb ending ي vs ـتُ). Keep the focus on the verb pair.

teach.heading: Explaining a change
bullets: تَغَيَّرَتْ عَلَاقَتِي بِأَخِي - my relationship with my brother changed
لِأَنَّنَا كَبِرْنَا - because we grew up
نَتَفَاهَمُ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ قَبْلُ - we understand each other more than before
teach.note: Higher-tier writing needs reasons. Teach لِأَنَّ + pronoun suffix (لِأَنَّنَا). Pupils write one sentence explaining a change. The 'more than before' chunk is useful for any then-and-now task.

practice: Say one sentence about your relationship with a parent.
Say what you used to do with a family member when you were young.
Translate: 'I used to argue with my sister but now we get on well.'
independent: Core: write 5 sentences about family relationships, then and now.
Extend: add reasons with لِأَنَّ and a sentence with أَكْثَرَ مِنْ قَبْلُ.
Stretch: write 100 words 'My family, then and now' using three tenses.
exit: Write: 'I used to play with my cousin.'
Write one sentence explaining why a relationship is better now.
lessons.homework: Write 80 words in Arabic about how your relationship with one family member has changed.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sentence frames for then/now and picture cards of family. Stretch: add a relative clause and a conditional (إِذَا).

lessons.unit: Unit 1.1: Who am I?
lessons.title: A good friend: qualities, family and time together
lessons.bigQuestion: What makes someone a good friend, and how do we spend time together?
objectives: Describe the character of friends and family
Explain what makes a good friend with reasons
Talk about interests and socialising with friends and family
successCriteria: All: say two qualities of a good friend
Most: describe a friend and say what you do together
Some: give reasons using لِأَنَّهُ and compare friends
lessons.crossCurricular: PSHE: healthy friendships
lessons.smsc: Moral: loyalty and honesty in friendship; choosing good company
starter: Retrieval: say 'my friend is tall and funny'.
Retrieval: say 'I used to play football with my cousin'.
Retrieval: say two things you do at the weekend.

teach.heading: Qualities of friends and family

head: Arabic
Transliteration
English
rows: my friend is honest and generous

teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Revise masculine and feminine adjectives. Ask pupils to describe one friend and one relative using these adjectives. The hadith that a person follows the way of his close friend, so look carefully at whom you befriend, is reported in Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi (verify the grading and wording before quoting).

teach.heading: What makes a good friend?
bullets: الصَّدِيقُ الْجَيِّدُ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيَّ - listens to me
يُسَاعِدُنِي عِنْدَمَا أَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ - helps me when I need him
لَا يَكْذِبُ عَلَيَّ - does not lie to me
teach.note: Pupils rank the four qualities and justify. Each verb is third person masculine present; for a female friend use the تَ prefix (تَسْتَمِعُ). Note the prepositions: يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَى, يَكْذِبُ عَلَى, يَحْتَاجُ إِلَى. These are common errors.

teach.heading: Interests and socialising
bullets: أَخْرُجُ مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِي يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ - I go out with friends on Saturdays
نَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ - we play football
تَجْتَمِعُ الْعَائِلَةُ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ - the family gets together on Friday
نَتَنَاوَلُ الْغَدَاءَ مَعًا - we have lunch together
teach.note: Connect to Jumuʿa and family gatherings (use only what is true for pupils). Practise question and answer: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ مَعَ أَصْدِقَائِكَ؟ Note تَجْتَمِعُ with a feminine singular subject (الْعَائِلَةُ) and أَصْدِقَائِي as a broken plural.

teach.heading: Model: describing a friend

model.problem: Write 3 sentences: 'My best friend is honest and generous. He listens to me. We play football together on Saturdays.'
steps: 'My best friend' = صَدِيقِي الْمُفَضَّلُ
'is honest and generous' = صَادِقٌ وَكَرِيمٌ
'He listens to me' = يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيَّ
'We play football together on Saturdays' = نَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ مَعًا يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ
model.answer: صَدِيقِي الْمُفَضَّلُ صَادِقٌ وَكَرِيمٌ. يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيَّ. نَلْعَبُ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ مَعًا يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ.

teach.note: Highlight that adjectives agree (masculine, indefinite) and that إِلَيَّ is إِلَى + ي. Then ask pupils to adapt it for a female friend (صَدِيقَتِي الْمُفَضَّلَةُ صَادِقَةٌ وَكَرِيمَةٌ، تَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيَّ).

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.why: يَسْتَمِعُ is 'listens' and إِلَيَّ is 'to me'. Pupils who choose B confuse it with يُسَاعِدُنِي.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Ask what the pronoun ending tells you (me). Use it to revisit the idea that Arabic verbs need the right preposition.

practice: Describe your best friend with two adjectives and a reason.
Say two things you do with your family at the weekend.
Translate: 'A good friend is honest because he does not lie.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about your friend and family (character and activities).
Extend: add 'what makes a good friend' with reasons using لِأَنَّ.
Stretch: write 100 words comparing two friends, with opinions.
exit: Write one quality of a good friend in Arabic.
Write what you do with friends at the weekend.
lessons.homework: Write 90 words in Arabic: 'My best friend and what we do together'.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: adjective cards with pictures and a sentence frame. Stretch: use two relative structures such as الصَّدِيقُ الَّذِي يَسْتَمِعُ.

lessons.unit: Unit 1.2: Daily life
lessons.title: Customs and everyday life at home
lessons.bigQuestion: What do our everyday habits and manners show about who we are?
objectives: Describe customs and manners at home
Talk about helping at home and welcoming guests
Use present-tense verbs with we and I
successCriteria: All: say two things you do at home
Most: describe a custom with a reason
Some: compare customs at home with customs in an Arabic-speaking country
lessons.crossCurricular: PSHE: responsibilities at home
lessons.smsc: Social and cultural: hospitality (ḍiyāfa) and good manners

keywords.def: we take off our shoes (nakhlaʿu l-ḥidhāʾ)

starter: Retrieval: say what time you wake up in Arabic.
Retrieval: name three meals in Arabic.
Retrieval: say 'my mother is caring' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Helping at home

head: Arabic
Transliteration
English
rows: I wash the dishes after dinner
I help my mother in the kitchen

teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Pupils choose the jobs they actually do. Note that بَعْدَ is followed by the genitive (الْعَشَاءِ). Ask how often: كُلَّ يَوْمٍ، أَحْيَانًا، فِي نِهَايَةِ الْأُسْبُوعِ.

teach.heading: Customs and manners
bullets: نَخْلَعُ الْحِذَاءَ عِنْدَ الْبَابِ - we take off shoes at the door
نَقُولُ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ - we say as-salāmu ʿalaykum
نَأْكُلُ بِالْيَدِ الْيُمْنَى - we eat with the right hand
نَقُولُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ قَبْلَ الْأَكْلِ - we say bismillah before eating
teach.note: Customs vary between homes, so invite pupils to say what is true for them. The Prophet taught the young Umar ibn Abi Salama to say Allah's name, eat with the right hand and eat from what is in front of him (Bukhari and Muslim). Keep it as manners (adab).

teach.heading: Hospitality
bullets: نُقَدِّمُ الشَّايَ أَوِ الْقَهْوَةَ لِلضُّيُوفِ - we serve tea or coffee to guests
الضِّيَافَةُ مُهِمَّةٌ فِي ثَقَافَتِنَا - hospitality is important in our culture
teach.note: In many Arabic-speaking homes it is usual to offer tea or coffee, sometimes with dates; describe this as common, not universal. Hadith: whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honour his guest (Bukhari and Muslim). Note الضُّيُوفُ is a broken plural of ضَيْف.

teach.heading: Model: customs in my house

model.problem: Translate: 'In my house we take off our shoes at the door. I help my mother and I wash the dishes after dinner.'
steps: 'In my house' = فِي بَيْتِنَا
'we take off our shoes at the door' = نَخْلَعُ الْحِذَاءَ عِنْدَ الْبَابِ
'I help my mother' = أُسَاعِدُ أُمِّي
'I wash the dishes after dinner' = أَغْسِلُ الْأَطْبَاقَ بَعْدَ الْعَشَاءِ
model.answer: فِي بَيْتِنَا نَخْلَعُ الْحِذَاءَ عِنْدَ الْبَابِ. أُسَاعِدُ أُمِّي وَأَغْسِلُ الْأَطْبَاقَ بَعْدَ الْعَشَاءِ.

teach.note: Show how to build from a place phrase, then 'we' verbs, then 'I' verbs. Note بَيْتِنَا (our house) is the genitive after فِي. Ask pupils to swap one detail to make it true for them.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.why: نُرَحِّبُ بِ means 'we welcome'. Pupils who choose B know the topic but not the verb.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Point out that the preposition بِ goes with نُرَحِّبُ.

practice: Say two jobs you do at home.
Say what you do before eating.
Translate: 'We usually welcome guests with tea.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about customs and everyday life in your home.
Extend: add reasons and frequencies.
Stretch: write 100 words comparing customs at home with those in an Arabic-speaking country (use only what you have learned).
exit: Write one custom in your home in Arabic.
Write one job you do at home.
lessons.homework: Write 80 words in Arabic about everyday customs in your home.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: picture cards for chores and manners, sentence frames. Stretch: use عِنْدَمَا and a conditional.

lessons.unit: Unit 1.2: Daily life
lessons.title: Food, drink and shopping in daily life
lessons.bigQuestion: How do we buy and talk about the food and drink we need every day?
objectives: Name everyday foods and drinks
Ask for quantities and prices
Shop for food using polite phrases
successCriteria: All: ask for two items
Most: ask for quantities and ask the price
Some: hold a short shop dialogue with a complaint or question
lessons.crossCurricular: Maths: money and quantities; PSHE: budgeting
lessons.smsc: Moral: buying what is lawful and good (ḥalāl and ṭayyib) and not wasting
starter: Retrieval: say 'I eat breakfast at seven'.
Retrieval: count to ten in Arabic.
Retrieval: say 'fruit is good for health'.

teach.heading: Food and drink
teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Revise from earlier lessons and add what is missing. Ask: what do you eat and drink every day? Add a halal angle: buying halal meat. Qur'an 2:168 tells people to eat what is lawful and good (verify the reference before displaying).

teach.heading: At the shop
bullets: أُرِيدُ كِيلُو مِنَ الْأَرُزِّ - I want a kilo of rice
عِنْدَكُمْ حَلِيبٌ؟ - do you have milk?
بِكَمْ هَذَا؟ - how much is this?
هَذَا كُلُّ شَيْءٍ، شُكْرًا - that is everything, thank you
teach.note: Teach the shop dialogue chunks. Note مِنَ + definite noun after a measure (كِيلُو مِنَ الْأَرُزِّ). Role-play shopkeeper and customer. Point out that عِنْدَكُمْ here means 'do you have' and is asked with rising intonation.

teach.heading: Prices

left.title: Asking
points: بِكَمْ الْكِيلُو؟ - how much is a kilo?
هَلْ هُنَاكَ خَصْمٌ؟ - is there a discount?

right.title: Answering
points: هَذَا غَالٍ جِدًّا - this is very expensive

teach.note: Currency varies by country; use the currency of the country you choose for the role play. Numbers 3 to 10 reverse the gender of the noun: masculine noun دِينَارٌ takes the form خَمْسَةُ with taa marbuta. Practise with three prices.

teach.heading: Model: a short shop dialogue

model.problem: Write: 'Good morning. I want a kilo of apples and a bottle of juice. How much is that? ... That is everything.'
steps: 'Good morning' = صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ
'I want a kilo of apples' = أُرِيدُ كِيلُو مِنَ التُّفَّاحِ
'and a bottle of juice' = وَزُجَاجَةَ عَصِيرٍ
'How much is that?' = بِكَمْ هَذَا؟
'That is everything' = هَذَا كُلُّ شَيْءٍ
model.answer: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ. أُرِيدُ كِيلُو مِنَ التُّفَّاحِ وَزُجَاجَةَ عَصِيرٍ. بِكَمْ هَذَا؟ ... هَذَا كُلُّ شَيْءٍ.

teach.note: Show the order: greeting, request, price, closing. Note the idāfa زُجَاجَةُ عَصِيرٍ: second noun indefinite genitive; here the first noun is accusative as the object of أُرِيدُ. Say that the answer is also a good spoken role-play script.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: What does أُرِيدُ كِيلُو مِنَ الْأَرُزِّ mean?
options: I want a kilo of rice
I sell a kilo of rice
I ate a kilo of rice
check.why: أُرِيدُ means 'I want'. D is a price question (بِكَمْ).

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Ask which word signals a request and which signals a price.

practice: Ask for a kilo of apples politely.
Ask how much the milk is.
Translate: 'The rice is cheap but the chicken is expensive.'
independent: Core: write a 6-line shop dialogue.
Extend: add a question about a discount and a thank-you.
Stretch: write 100 words about food shopping with your family, with an opinion.
exit: Write how to ask the price in Arabic.
Write one item you want to buy and the quantity.
lessons.homework: Write a 6-line dialogue between a customer and a shopkeeper in Arabic.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: picture menu, price cards, sentence frames. Stretch: add comparatives (أَرْخَصُ مِنْ).

lessons.unit: Unit 1.3: Cultural life
lessons.title: Sport: teams, matches and results
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do sport and teams bring people together?
objectives: Talk about watching and following sport
Describe a match and its result in the past tense
Express opinions about sport and sportsmanship
successCriteria: All: say what sport you watch
Most: report a result in the past tense
Some: give an opinion about a sport with reasons
lessons.crossCurricular: PE: team sport and fair play
lessons.smsc: Moral and social: good sportsmanship and respect for opponents
starter: Retrieval: say 'I play football three times a week'.
Retrieval: say 'sport is good for health'.
Retrieval: say what you did yesterday.

teach.heading: Teams and matches

head: Arabic
Transliteration
English
rows: I watch the match on TV

teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Ask pupils what they watch. Use sport pupils actually follow (football, cricket, boxing). Note مُشَاهَدَة (watching) vs لَعِبَ (playing). Keep the vocabulary at GCSE level.

teach.heading: Reporting a result
bullets: خَسِرَ الْفَرِيقُ الْآخَرُ - the other team lost
تَعَادَلَ الْفَرِيقَانِ - the two teams drew
سَجَّلَ اللَّاعِبُ هَدَفًا - the player scored a goal
teach.note: These are third-person past-tense verbs, the typical form in a match report. Note the dual الْفَرِيقَانِ (two teams) takes a masculine singular verb here. The word 'against' can be مُقَابِلَ: فَازَ فَرِيقُنَا بِثَلَاثَةِ أَهْدَافٍ مُقَابِلَ هَدَفٍ (won by three goals to one).

teach.heading: Model: a short match report

model.problem: Write: 'Yesterday I watched the match. Our team won by three goals to one. I was very happy.'
steps: 'Yesterday I watched the match' = أَمْسِ شَاهَدْتُ الْمُبَارَاةَ
'Our team won' = فَازَ فَرِيقُنَا
'by three goals to one' = بِثَلَاثَةِ أَهْدَافٍ مُقَابِلَ هَدَفٍ
'I was very happy' = كُنْتُ سَعِيدًا جِدًّا
model.answer: أَمْسِ شَاهَدْتُ الْمُبَارَاةَ. فَازَ فَرِيقُنَا بِثَلَاثَةِ أَهْدَافٍ مُقَابِلَ هَدَفٍ. كُنْتُ سَعِيدًا جِدًّا.

teach.note: Point out the numerals: ثَلَاثَةُ with masculine plural أَهْدَافٌ in the genitive. Ask pupils to change the result. Female pupils say سَعِيدَةً.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.why: خَسِرَ means 'lost'. Pupils who choose B may confuse it with فَازَ.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Ask for the Arabic for the other three.

teach.heading: Opinions and sportsmanship
bullets: الرُّوحُ الرِّيَاضِيَّةُ مُهِمَّةٌ - sportsmanship is important
أُحِبُّ كُرَةَ الْقَدَمِ لِأَنَّهَا تَجْمَعُ النَّاسَ - I like football because it brings people together
لَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ نَغْضَبَ عِنْدَ الْخَسَارَةِ - we should not get angry when losing
teach.note: Pupils give an opinion. The Prophet (peace be upon him) is reported to have raced with Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) (Abu Dawud; verify grading before quoting). Link to respect for opponents.

practice: Say which team or sport you follow and why.
Report a result in two sentences.
Translate: 'The match ended and my team lost.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about a match you watched.
Extend: add opinions with لِأَنَّ and a sentence about sportsmanship.
Stretch: write 100 words comparing playing sport with watching sport.
exit: Write one match result in Arabic.
Write one reason why sport is important.
lessons.homework: Write a 90-word match report in Arabic.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: matching cards of results; sentence frames. Stretch: use the passive (هُزِمَ الْفَرِيقُ) with teacher support.

hook.text: You are in Madinah and need to find the masjid of Quba'. What questions would you ask, and what words would you listen for?
hook.a: Ask how to get there and how far; listen for right, left, straight on and distances.

islamicLink.text: Allah names the traveller (ابْنُ السَّبِيلِ) among those owed help (al-Baqarah 2:177). Giving directions kindly helps a traveller.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'There is not': A) لَا يُوجَدُ B) يُوجَدُ

teach.heading: Asking the way

head: Arabic
English
rows: excuse me, how do I get to the station?

teach.note: Begin with bismillah. أَقْرَبُ + indefinite noun = the nearest ... .

teach.heading: The imperative for three listeners
teach.note: Woman: ـِي; group: ـُوا (with a silent alif).

teach.heading: Model: a route

model.problem: From the station to the masjid (to a woman).
steps: اُخْرُجِي مِنَ المَحَطَّةِ وَاِمْشِي مُسْتَقِيمًا.
عِنْدَ إِشَارَةِ المُرُورِ اِنْعَطِفِي يَسَارًا.
خُذِي الشَّارِعَ الثَّانِيَ عَلَى اليَمِينِ.
المَسْجِدُ أَمَامَ الحَدِيقَةِ.
model.answer: Four steps, feminine imperative

teach.note: أَمَامَ (in front of), خَلْفَ (behind), بَيْنَ (between), مُقَابِلَ (opposite).

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: Group: ـُوا: اِنْعَطِفُوا.

practice.q: Give a man directions: go straight on, then take the first street on the left.
practice.a: اِذْهَبْ مُسْتَقِيمًا، ثُمَّ خُذِ الشَّارِعَ الأَوَّلَ عَلَى اليَسَارِ.
practice.model:
Man: اِذْهَبْ مُسْتَقِيمًا.
ثُمَّ.
خُذْ → خُذِ before al-: خُذِ الشَّارِعَ الأَوَّلَ عَلَى اليَسَارِ.

practice.q: Ask: Where is the nearest masjid?
Translate: It is ten minutes' walk away.

independent.q: Core: Using the town map (worksheet), write directions for three routes: one to a man, one to a woman, one to a group.
independent.a: Marked for correct imperative forms, place words and prepositions.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first route to a man, tracing it on the map.

independent.q: Extend: Write a four-line dialogue: a visitor asks the way and how far; you answer.
independent.a: For example: عَفْوًا، كَيْفَ أَصِلُ إِلَى المَكْتَبَةِ؟ اِذْهَبْ مُسْتَقِيمًا ثُمَّ اِنْعَطِفْ يَمِينًا. هَلْ هِيَ بَعِيدَةٌ؟ لَا، عَلَى بُعْدِ خَمْسِ دَقَائِقَ.

independent.q: Stretch: Say 'do not turn left' (to a man) with لَا النَّاهِيَة.
independent.a: لَا تَنْعَطِفْ يَسَارًا.

exit.q: 'Take' to a woman: A) خُذِي B) خُذْ C) خُذُوا
Big question: ask the way and give one direction in Arabic.
exit.a: For example: كَيْفَ أَصِلُ إِلَى المَحَطَّةِ؟ اِذْهَبْ مُسْتَقِيمًا.

lessons.unit: Unit 2.2: Travel and tourist transactions
lessons.title: Eating out and shopping on holiday
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I book a table, order, pay and shop confidently in an Arabic-speaking country?
objectives: Book a table and order food
Ask for the bill and pay
Buy gifts and deal with a problem politely
successCriteria: All: order a meal and ask for the bill
Most: book a table and ask about a dish
Some: make a polite complaint and buy a gift
lessons.crossCurricular: Business: customer service; PSHE: being polite
lessons.smsc: Moral: courtesy in dealing with others
starter: Retrieval: ask for a kilo of rice.
Retrieval: say 'I want water and bread'.
Retrieval: say 'it is very expensive'.

teach.heading: At the restaurant

head: Arabic
Transliteration
English
rows: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَحْجِزَ طَاوِلَةً لِأَرْبَعَةِ أَشْخَاصٍ
urīdu an aḥjiza ṭāwilatan li-arbaʿati ashkhāṣ
I want to book a table for four people

teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Note أَنْ + subjunctive (أَحْجِزَ). Numbers: لِأَرْبَعَةِ أَشْخَاصٍ (the number takes the form with taa marbuta before a masculine plural). Practise with different group sizes. Asking if food is halal is a real need when travelling.

teach.heading: Ordering and problems
bullets: أُرِيدُ دَجَاجًا وَأَرُزًّا - I want chicken and rice
أُفَضِّلُ الْعَصِيرَ عَلَى الْقَهْوَةِ - I prefer juice to coffee
الشَّوْرَبَةُ بَارِدَةٌ - the soup is cold
هَذَا لَيْسَ مَا طَلَبْتُهُ - this is not what I ordered
teach.note: Teach أُفَضِّلُ ... عَلَى ... (prefer ... to ...). Complaints must stay polite: add عَفْوًا at the start. The soup (شَوْرَبَةٌ) is feminine so the adjective is feminine (بَارِدَةٌ).

teach.heading: Shopping for gifts
bullets: هَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ هَدَايَا؟ - do you have gifts?
أُرِيدُ هَدِيَّةً لِأُمِّي - I want a gift for my mother
هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ أَدْفَعَ بِالْبِطَاقَةِ؟ - can I pay by card?
هَذَا غَالٍ جِدًّا - this is very expensive
teach.note: Teach هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ + subjunctive for polite requests. The plural of هَدِيَّةٌ is هَدَايَا (diptote). Exam tasks often mix eating out and shopping in one role play, so practise switching.

teach.heading: Model: restaurant role play

model.problem: Role play: you want a table for two, you order fish and water, and you ask for the bill.
steps: Table: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَحْجِزَ طَاوِلَةً لِشَخْصَيْنِ
Order: أُرِيدُ سَمَكًا وَمَاءً
Bill: الْحِسَابُ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ
Close: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا
model.answer: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَحْجِزَ طَاوِلَةً لِشَخْصَيْنِ. أُرِيدُ سَمَكًا وَمَاءً. الْحِسَابُ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.

teach.note: Show the sequence: book, order, pay, thank. The dual لِشَخْصَيْنِ means 'for two people' (no number word needed). In the exam, answer every part of the role-play prompt and ask any question requested. Arabic specialist to check the dual form.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which is the polite way to ask for the bill?
check.why: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ means 'please'. B is a command, C asks where it is and D says it is expensive.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Discuss register: politeness is rewarded in role plays and reflects adab.

practice: Book a table for three people.
Order a meal and ask for the bill.
Translate: 'I want a gift for my sister. Can I pay by card?'
independent: Core: write a 6-line restaurant dialogue.
Extend: add a polite complaint.
Stretch: write 100 words about a meal and shopping trip on holiday.
exit: Write how to ask for the bill politely.
Write one thing you would order.
lessons.homework: Write a 6-line dialogue in Arabic: you are buying a gift and then eating out.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: dialogue cards and a menu with pictures. Stretch: add أُفَضِّلُ and a comparison.

lessons.title: Weather and plans; unit quiz
lessons.bigQuestion: How does the weather change what we do, and how much of this half term's Arabic can I now use?
objectives: To understand how to describe weather and forecasts and link them to plans, then show the unit's learning in a quiz
successCriteria: All: describe the weather and the temperature
Most: give a forecast with سَيَكُونُ + accusative
Some: link weather to plans with إِذَا كَانَ ... فَسَـ ...
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: weather and climate
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: rain as a mercy; gratitude whatever the weather

hook.text: British weather is famous for being changeable. How do you plan a weekend when you cannot be sure of the weather?
hook.a: Make plans for both: if sunny ..., if rainy ...; and say in sha' Allah.

islamicLink.text: Allah sends down rain from the sky as a blessing and brings life to the earth with it (Qaf 50:9). Muslims thank Allah for rain and every kind of weather.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'On the other hand': A) مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى B) بِالرَّغْمِ مِنْ

teach.heading: Weather

head: Arabic
English
rows: the weather in Britain is changeable

teach.note: Begin with bismillah. دَرَجَة is feminine: خَمْسُ دَرَجَاتٍ; 11 and above: عِشْرُونَ دَرَجَةً.

teach.heading: Forecasts
teach.note: سَيَكُونُ + accusative predicate (مُمْطِرًا).

teach.heading: Weather and plans
teach.note: إِذَا + past verb (future meaning) + فَـ + future.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: The predicate of كَانَ / يَكُونُ is accusative: بَارِدًا.

practice.q: Write a plan: if it is windy, we will read at home.
practice.a: إِذَا كَانَتِ الرِّيَاحُ قَوِيَّةً فَسَنَقْرَأُ فِي البَيْتِ.
practice.model:
إِذَا كَانَتِ (feminine for الرِّيَاحُ).
الرِّيَاحُ قَوِيَّةً (accusative predicate).
فَسَنَقْرَأُ فِي البَيْتِ.

practice.q: Translate: The temperature is twenty degrees.

independent.q: Core (unit quiz, Forms): 1) Translate: my town is in the north of England. 2) 'There is no airport in my town'. 3) Imperative to a woman: تَنْعَطِفُ. 4) 'It will be rainy tomorrow'. 5) Correct the error: يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَزُورُ المَتْحَفَ. 6) Write two sentences giving a balanced view of your town.
independent.a: 1) تَقَعُ مَدِينَتِي فِي شَمَالِ إِنْجِلْتِرَا. 2) لَا يُوجَدُ مَطَارٌ فِي مَدِينَتِي. 3) اِنْعَطِفِي 4) سَيَكُونُ الجَوُّ مُمْطِرًا غَدًا. 5) تَزُورَ 6) For example: مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ، مَدِينَتِي جَمِيلَةٌ، وَمِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى، فِيهَا اِزْدِحَامٌ.
independent.model: Teacher does question 3 aloud: woman, so ـِي: اِنْعَطِفِي.

independent.q: Extend: Write a weekend weather forecast for your town with two plans using إِذَا.
independent.a: For example: سَيَكُونُ الجَوُّ غَائِمًا يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ. إِذَا أَمْطَرَتِ السَّمَاءُ فَسَأَزُورُ المَكْتَبَةَ.

independent.q: Stretch (Group A): give the i'rab of مُمْطِرًا in سَيَكُونُ الجَوُّ مُمْطِرًا.
independent.a: خَبَرُ يَكُونُ مَنْصُوبٌ وَعَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ الفَتْحَةُ

exit.q: What is النَّشْرَةُ الجَوِّيَّةُ? A) weather forecast B) temperature C) rain
Big question: which skill from this half term are you most confident with, and which needs work? Write one target.
exit.a: Pupils' own target (for example: the subjunctive after أَنْ).

lessons.homework: Correct your quiz in green pen and write three new sentences using the point you got wrong.

lessons.unit: Unit 2.3: Town, region and country
lessons.title: Places to see and things to do in a region
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I persuade someone to visit a region, and what can they do there?
objectives: Describe places to see in a region or country
Suggest things to do
Recommend a place with reasons
successCriteria: All: name two places to see
Most: say two things to do there
Some: recommend a place with reasons and a past-tense visit
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: tourism and landscape
lessons.smsc: Cultural: appreciating creation and heritage
starter: Retrieval: say 'it will be sunny tomorrow'.
Retrieval: turn left and go straight (in Arabic).
Retrieval: say 'there is a museum but no beach'.

teach.heading: Places to see
teach.note: Arabic specialist to check: all Arabic, vowelling and transliteration in this lesson before delivery. Begin with bismillah. Use British and Arabic-world examples your pupils know. Note that non-human plurals take feminine singular adjectives: جِبَالٌ عَالِيَةٌ. Qur'an: reflect on Allah's creation; do not quote a verse unless verified by the staff.

teach.heading: Things to do
bullets: أَتَجَوَّلُ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ الْقَدِيمَةِ - I stroll round the old city
أَلْتَقِطُ صُوَرًا جَمِيلَةً - I take beautiful photos
teach.note: Present tense for general activity. Give pupils the choice of subject: يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَتَسَلَّقَ (you can climb). Draw attention to the long vowel in صُوَرًا (plural of صُورَةٌ) and ask pupils to say it aloud.

teach.heading: Recommending
bullets: أَنْصَحُكَ بِزِيَارَةِ وَيْلْزَ - I recommend visiting Wales
لِأَنَّهَا جَمِيلَةٌ وَهَادِئَةٌ - because it is beautiful and quiet
زُرْتُهَا الصَّيْفَ الْمَاضِيَ - I visited it last summer
teach.note: Teach أَنْصَحُكَ بِ + masdar (visiting). Note لِأَنَّهَا refers back to Wales (feminine). Past-tense recount: زُرْتُهَا (I visited it). Pupils recommend a real place they know.

teach.heading: Model: a recommendation

model.problem: Write: 'Wales has high mountains and old castles. You can climb the mountains and visit the castles. I recommend it because it is beautiful.'
steps: 'Wales has high mountains and old castles' = فِي وَيْلْزَ جِبَالٌ عَالِيَةٌ وَقِلَاعٌ قَدِيمَةٌ
'You can climb the mountains' = يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَتَسَلَّقَ الْجِبَالَ
'and visit the castles' = وَأَنْ تَزُورَ الْقِلَاعَ
'I recommend it because it is beautiful' = أَنْصَحُكَ بِزِيَارَتِهَا لِأَنَّهَا جَمِيلَةٌ
model.answer: فِي وَيْلْزَ جِبَالٌ عَالِيَةٌ وَقِلَاعٌ قَدِيمَةٌ. يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَتَسَلَّقَ الْجِبَالَ وَأَنْ تَزُورَ الْقِلَاعَ. أَنْصَحُكَ بِزِيَارَتِهَا لِأَنَّهَا جَمِيلَةٌ.

teach.note: Check the order: place, things to do, recommendation, reason. Arabic specialist to check the plurals قِلَاعٌ and جِبَالٌ and the spelling of the place name.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which means 'You can climb the mountains'?
check.why: يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ + subjunctive means 'you can'. B means 'live in', C mixes present and yesterday, D is a prohibition.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. Keep the focus on يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ.

practice: Name two places to see in a region you know.
Say what a visitor can do there.
Translate: 'I recommend visiting the old city because it is interesting.'
independent: Core: write 6 sentences about places to see and things to do in a region.
Extend: add a recommendation with a reason.
Stretch: write 100 words persuading a visitor, including a past visit.
exit: Write one thing you can do in your region.
Write one reason to recommend it.
lessons.homework: Write a 90-word tourist leaflet about a region of Britain.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: picture cards with captions and sentence frames. Stretch: use a relative clause with الَّتِي.

lessons.title: My town and region: where it is and what it is like
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I describe where I live so that a reader can picture it?
objectives: To understand how to describe the location and character of a town and region in Arabic
successCriteria: All: say where my town is: تَقَعُ مَدِينَتِي فِي ...
Most: describe it with three adjectives and a reason
Some: compare town and region with a comparative
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: location, compass points and settlement types
lessons.smsc: Social: belonging to a local community and its masjid

hook.text: If a visitor from Egypt asked what your town is like, which three words would you choose and why?
hook.a: Any three adjectives with reasons; today we build them in Arabic.

islamicLink.text: Allah tells us to travel through the land and observe (al-'Ankabut 29:20). Describing places carefully is part of reflecting on His creation and human life.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'I fasted': A) صُمْتُ B) صَامْتُ
Name three places in a town in Arabic.

teach.heading: Where is it?

head: Arabic
English
rows: my town is in the north of England
in the south / east / west / centre of ...
the capital of Britain is London

teach.note: Begin with bismillah. مَدِينَة is feminine: تَقَعُ. For a masculine place (بَلَد): يَقَعُ.

teach.heading: What is it like?
teach.note: All in the feminine to agree with مَدِينَة.

teach.heading: Town and countryside
teach.note: Comparatives from Year 8: أَهْدَأُ (quieter), أَنْظَفُ (cleaner); أَكْثَرُ + noun for longer adjectives.

teach.heading: Model: a description

model.problem: صِفْ مَدِينَتَكَ.
steps: أَسْكُنُ فِي بِرْمِنْغْهَام، وَهِيَ مَدِينَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ تَقَعُ فِي وَسَطِ إِنْجِلْتِرَا.
مَدِينَتِي حَدِيثَةٌ وَمُزْدَحِمَةٌ، وَفِيهَا مَسَاجِدُ كَثِيرَةٌ.
الرِّيفُ أَهْدَأُ مِنَ المَدِينَةِ، لٰكِنِّي أُفَضِّلُ المَدِينَةَ لِأَنَّ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قَرِيبٌ.
model.answer: Location, character, comparison and preference

teach.note: Note وَهِيَ to add information.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: مَدِينَة is feminine: هَادِئَةٌ. أَهْدَأُ means quieter.

practice.q: Say: Leeds is in the north of England and it is a historic city.
practice.a: تَقَعُ لِيدْز فِي شَمَالِ إِنْجِلْتِرَا، وَهِيَ مَدِينَةٌ تَارِيخِيَّةٌ.
practice.model:
تَقَعُ (feminine, a city).
لِيدْز فِي شَمَالِ إِنْجِلْتِرَا.
Add: وَهِيَ مَدِينَةٌ تَارِيخِيَّةٌ.

practice.q: Comparative of نَظِيف?
What is مِنْطَقَة?

independent.q: Core: Write 80 words (portal response box) describing your town or region: location, three adjectives, places, a comparison with the countryside and your preference.
independent.a: Marked for location phrases, feminine agreement, comparison, preference with reason.
independent.model: Teacher writes a location sentence and one description sentence for a different town.

independent.q: Extend: Translate into Arabic: My region is beautiful but the town centre is crowded at the weekend.
independent.a: مِنْطَقَتِي جَمِيلَةٌ لٰكِنَّ وَسَطَ المَدِينَةِ مُزْدَحِمٌ فِي نِهَايَةِ الأُسْبُوعِ.

independent.q: Stretch (Group A): explain why وَسَطَ is accusative in your translation.
independent.a: اِسْمُ لٰكِنَّ مَنْصُوبٌ (the noun after لٰكِنَّ is accusative)

exit.q: 'Is located in' (for a city): A) تَقَعُ فِي B) يَقَعُ فِي
Big question: describe your town in one developed sentence.
exit.a: For example: أَسْكُنُ فِي مَدِينَةٍ هَادِئَةٍ تَقَعُ فِي جَنُوبِ إِنْجِلْتِرَا.

lessons.title: Directions in the exam: role play and the imperative explained
lessons.bigQuestion: How is the imperative formed, and how do I use it under exam conditions?
objectives: To understand how the imperative is formed from the present tense and use it in exam-style tasks
successCriteria: All: complete a 1AA0-style role play on directions
Most: form the imperative from a present verb in three steps
Some: give the grammatical ruling (بِنَاء) of an imperative using Arabic terms
lessons.crossCurricular: English: grammar terminology (imperative, mood)
lessons.smsc: Cultural: the Arabic grammatical tradition and its terms

keywords.def: fixed by dropping the nun (e.g. اِذْهَبُوا)
the joining alif at the start of اِذْهَبْ

hook.text: تَذْهَبُ means 'you go'. How could you turn it into the order 'Go!' by removing and adding letters?
hook.a: Drop تَـ, the end becomes sukun, add a joining alif: اِذْهَبْ.

islamicLink.text: The first word revealed to the Prophet ﷺ was an imperative: اِقْرَأْ, 'Read!' (al-'Alaq 96:1). It is formed exactly as we learn today.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'Go' to a woman: A) اِذْهَبِي B) اِذْهَبُوا
Ask 'how do I get to the station?'

teach.heading: Forming the imperative

model.problem: From تَذْهَبُ to اِذْهَبْ
steps: Start with 'you' present: تَذْهَبُ
Make it jussive (sukun): تَذْهَبْ
Drop the تَـ: ذْهَبْ
Cannot start with sukun: add hamzat al-wasl: اِذْهَبْ
model.answer: اِذْهَبْ

teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Same steps: تَكْتُبُ → اُكْتُبْ (a dammah verb takes اُ), تَقْرَأُ → اِقْرَأْ.

teach.heading: Its ruling (for Group A)
teach.note: The imperative is always مَبْنِيّ (fixed), never مُعْرَب. 4AA1 Paper 1 grammar questions use these terms.

teach.heading: 'Do not': لَا النَّاهِيَة
bullets: لَا + jussive: لَا تَذْهَبْ (do not go)
لَا تَتَأَخَّرُوا (do not be late, to a group)
teach.note: The verb is مَجْزُوم after لَا النَّاهِيَة.

teach.heading: Role play (Group B, 1AA0 style)
bullets: You are a tourist. Ask: the way to the museum
Respond to the unexpected question (!) and say thank you
teach.note: Teacher plays the local. Unexpected question: مَاذَا سَتَفْعَلُ فِي المَتْحَفِ؟ Pupils answer in the future.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: The middle vowel of يَكْتُبُ is dammah, so the joining alif takes dammah: اُكْتُبْ.

practice.q: Form the imperative (to a man) of تَجْلِسُ.
practice.model:
تَجْلِسُ → jussive تَجْلِسْ.
Drop تَـ: جْلِسْ.
Add hamzat al-wasl with kasrah: اِجْلِسْ.

practice.q: Say 'do not cross the road' (تَعْبُرُ) to a man.
Ruling of اِنْعَطِفُوا?

independent.q: Core: Exam-style grammar (portal quiz): form the imperative to a man and a woman of تَدْخُلُ، تَفْتَحُ، تَقْرَأُ، تَمْشِي.
independent.a: اُدْخُلْ / اُدْخُلِي؛ اِفْتَحْ / اِفْتَحِي؛ اِقْرَأْ / اِقْرَئِي؛ اِمْشِ / اِمْشِي
independent.model: Teacher does تَدْخُلُ: dammah verb, so اُدْخُلْ; feminine اُدْخُلِي.

independent.q: Extend (Group B): perform the role play in a breakout pair, then swap roles; record (audio only) for teacher feedback.
independent.a: Role play with all bullet points covered and the unexpected question answered

independent.q: Stretch (Group A): give the full i'rab of اِقْرَأْ in اِقْرَأِ النَّصَّ.
independent.a: فِعْلُ أَمْرٍ مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى السُّكُونِ، وَحُرِّكَ بِالكَسْرِ لِالْتِقَاءِ السَّاكِنَيْنِ؛ وَالفَاعِلُ ضَمِيرٌ مُسْتَتِرٌ تَقْدِيرُهُ أَنْتَ

exit.q: The imperative is always: A) مَبْنِيّ B) مُعْرَب
Big question: how is the imperative formed?
exit.a: From the jussive 'you' present: drop the تَـ and add a joining alif if the word starts with sukun.

lessons.title: My town: good points and problems; a balanced view
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I write a balanced argument about where I live and suggest improvements?
objectives: To understand how to present advantages, problems and solutions about a town in a balanced paragraph
successCriteria: All: name three advantages and three problems
Most: link them with مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ ... وَمِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى
Some: suggest a solution with يَجِبُ أَنْ / عَلَى ... أَنْ
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: urban problems: congestion, pollution and housing
lessons.smsc: Moral: responsibility for our community and environment

hook.text: What one change would make your town better for young people? Who should make it happen?
hook.a: Any answer with a reason; today we argue it in Arabic.

islamicLink.text: Allah warns that corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what people's hands have earned (ar-Rum 30:41). Caring for our towns and environment is part of being khalifah on earth.

starter.q: Bismillah. 'Do not go': A) لَا تَذْهَبْ B) لَا تَذْهَبُ
'There is a museum in my town'?

teach.heading: Good points and problems
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Pupils add one of each for their own town.

teach.heading: Balancing phrases
teach.note: These phrases score for range in 1AA0 Paper 4 and 4AA1 Paper 2.

teach.heading: Suggesting solutions
bullets: عَلَى البَلَدِيَّةِ أَنْ تَبْنِيَ مَرَاكِزَ لِلشَّبَابِ
مِنَ المُهِمِّ أَنْ نُحَافِظَ عَلَى نَظَافَةِ الشَّوَارِعِ
teach.note: All followed by أَنْ + subjunctive (fathah).

teach.heading: Model: a balanced paragraph

model.problem: مَا رَأْيُكَ فِي مَدِينَتِكَ؟
steps: مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ، مَدِينَتِي حَيَوِيَّةٌ وَالمَوَاصَلَاتُ فِيهَا جَيِّدَةٌ.
وَمِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى، هُنَاكَ اِزْدِحَامٌ وَتَلَوُّثٌ فِي وَسَطِ المَدِينَةِ.
فِي رَأْيِي، يَجِبُ عَلَى البَلَدِيَّةِ أَنْ تَزْرَعَ أَشْجَارًا أَكْثَرَ.
بِالرَّغْمِ مِنْ ذٰلِكَ، أُحِبُّ مَدِينَتِي لِأَنَّ أُسْرَتِي هُنَا.
model.answer: Positive, negative, solution, conclusion

teach.note: Label the four moves.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى = on the other hand.

practice.q: Write a solution to traffic congestion with يَجِبُ أَنْ.
practice.a: For example: يَجِبُ أَنْ نَمْشِيَ أَوْ نَرْكَبَ الدَّرَّاجَاتِ بَدَلًا مِنَ السَّيَّارَاتِ.
practice.model:
Start: يَجِبُ أَنْ.
Verb in the subjunctive: نَمْشِيَ (fathah).
Alternative: بَدَلًا مِنَ السَّيَّارَاتِ.

practice.q: Translate: Despite the noise, I like my town.

independent.q: Core: Write 100 to 120 words (portal response box): مَدِينَتِي: إِيجَابِيَّاتٌ وَسَلْبِيَّاتٌ. Include two positives, two problems, a solution and a conclusion.
independent.a: Marked as a Paper 4 / Paper 2 style task: content, range (balancing phrases, subjunctive), accuracy.
independent.model: Teacher plans aloud with the four moves and writes the opening sentence.

independent.q: Extend (Group A, 4AA1 summary skill): read the model paragraph and summarise it in 25 Arabic words in your own words.
independent.a: For example: يَرَى الكَاتِبُ أَنَّ مَدِينَتَهُ حَيَوِيَّةٌ لٰكِنَّ فِيهَا اِزْدِحَامًا وَتَلَوُّثًا، وَيَقْتَرِحُ زِرَاعَةَ الأَشْجَارِ، وَيُحِبُّهَا لِأَنَّ أُسْرَتَهُ هُنَاكَ.

independent.q: Stretch: Add a sentence in the future about how your town will be in ten years.
independent.a: For example: بَعْدَ عَشْرِ سَنَوَاتٍ سَتَكُونُ مَدِينَتِي أَنْظَفَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰهُ.

exit.q: What is تَلَوُّث? A) pollution B) congestion C) noise
Big question: what makes an argument balanced?
exit.a: Both positives and negatives, linked with balancing phrases, then a reasoned conclusion or solution.

lessons.send: SEND: four-box writing frame. EAL: positives and negatives word bank. Stretch: add a conditional: لَوْ كُنْتُ رَئِيسَ البَلَدِيَّةِ لَبَنَيْتُ ...

quote.text:
أَسْكُنُ فِي مَدِينَةِ بِرْمِنْغْهَام. هِيَ مَدِينَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ فِيهَا مَسَاجِدُ كَثِيرَةٌ وَمَكْتَبَاتٌ.

Where does the grandfather live?
